item.title: Even Microsoft Execs Are Annoyed by Terrible AI-Generated Work
item.description:
Source: PCMag Score: 2.19
A LinkedIn exec is fed up with AI slop, which might strike some as ironic given that LinkedIn itself has struggled to keep AI content in check. In a recent post, Ryan Roslansky, a Microsoft EVP responsible for LinkedIn, Microsoft Office, Outlook, and Teams, complained that someone had sent him "what was clearly an AI-generated doc." After realizing it was AI, he actually asked his AI to summarize it, "and ended up with nothing that brought new thinking to the idea." This, he argues, is "a doom loop" that could leave us with "a very expensive way to avoid writing and reading in an ocean of sameness, genericness." Microsoft has pushed its Copilot AI hard, to the point that it recently pulled back on some integrations following complaints. On LinkedIn, the influx of AI tools has led to a flood of AI slop posts. It got bad enough that LinkedIn added a feature where you can click to report something that "seems like AI slop." (And over a million people have taken advantage of that button.) But while execs like Roslansky and Xbox CEO Asha Sharma have bemoaned "soulless AI slop," Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella is not a fan of that characterization. "We need to get beyond the arguments of slop vs sophistication," he said in March. Still, Roslansky's LinkedIn post earned the thumbs-up from fellow Microsoft employees, including President Brad Smith. Roslansky is unlikely to ditch AI. He released a book in March, titled Open to Work, about how to make the most of AI in the workplace. (Presumably, one of the rules is to avoid maxing out your tokens.) But he's correct that replacing human communication with AI summaries is no way to run an organization. He also touches on a real concern of AI regression: who wants to read things that sound exactly the same? About Our Expert Jon Martindale is a tech journalist from the UK, with 20 years of experience covering all manner of PC components and associated gadgets. He's written for a range of publications, including ExtremeTech, Digital Trends, Forbes, U.S. News & World Report, and Lifewire, among others. When not writing, he's a big board gamer and reader, with a particular habit of speed-reading through long manga sagas. Jon covers the latest PC components, as well as how-to guides on everything from how to take a screenshot to how to set up your cryptocurrency wallet. He particularly enjoys the battles between the top tech giants in CPUs and GPUs, and tries his best not to take sides. Jon's gaming PC is built around the iconic 7950X3D CPU, with a 7900XTX backing it up. That's all the power he needs to play lightweight indie and casual games, as well as more demanding sim titles like Kerbal Space Program. He uses a pair of Jabra Active 8 earbuds and a SteelSeries Arctis Pro wireless headset, and types all day on a Logitech G915 mechanical keyboard.

item.title: Claude’s updated Fable and Mythos models watermark their replies
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Score: 8.14
Anthropic has announced the arrival of its latest Claude models, and just as it promised last month, the new models will add invisible watermarks to all their text replies. Claude Fable 5.1 is now generally available in the Claude desktop app and other platforms, while Claude Mythos 5.1 is restricted to Anthropic’s “trusted access program.” While both models are the same, Mythos lands with less stringent safeguards to “support work in cybersecurity and the life sciences.” In its announcement, Anthropic shows off a variety of benchmarks demonstrating the performance boosts the two models, complete with double-digit increases when it comes to agentic scientific research, agentic coding, and business workflows. Anthropic also says both Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 were evaluated using the company’s new safety and alignment procedures, developed in response to Anthropic’s disclosures of Claude models hacking outside companies during internal testing. Specifically, Mythos 5.1 is “less likely than Mythos 5 to try to access resources outside of its test environment when assigned an otherwise impossible task,” Anthropic said. Beyond their agentic capabilities and upgraded safeguards, through, Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 mark the first Claude models to watermark their text and file outputs, in accordance with the EU AI Act. “As we recently explained, this watermark is invisible to anyone who does not have the detection API,” Anthropic wrote in its announcement. “It has no practical impact on the quality or content of Claude’s outputs and contains no information about the user, their organization, or their conversations with Claude.” As for the detection API, Anthropic says is now available to regulators, law enforcement, media, fact-checkers, independent researches, and other “eligible groups” as defined by the just-enacted EU law, adding that it will “expand access to the detection API over time.” You can apply for access to the API via this signup form. Anthropic had previously stated it would add watermark support to any new Claude models released after August 2, 2026. Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 are the first new Claude models to arrive subsequent to that date, while older Claude models will eventually add watermarking support as well, Anthropic has previously said. Claude text watermarking works by “nudging” the model’s word choices during the inference process, meaning the model might pick one word over another in cases where there are multiple likely options. Designed to survive a copy-and-paste as well as light editing, the watermarks are invisible, but the text patterns can be pinpointed using Anthropic’s detection API. While the presence of a Claude text watermark would show that a piece of text had been either written or “processed” by Claude, the absence of a watermark doesn’t necessarily mean the text was written by a human.

item.title: Everyone assumed the Windows taskbar copied a rival OS. Microsoft says no
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Score: 6.13
In a recent social media thread, Microsoft veterans Brad Silverberg, Joe Belfiore, and Dave Plummer shared a few anecdotes and clarifications about how the taskbar became part of Windows. The taskbar, first introduced with Windows 95, allowed users to keep track of multiple active programs simultaneously, making it one of the highlight features of the cutting-edge operating system. But the foundation for the Windows taskbar was laid in “Cairo,” a Microsoft project launched back in 1991. In Cairo, “fields” were located at the bottom of the screen and were always visible. In developing the Windows 95 taskbar, the Cairo design was combined with a feature from Windows 3.1 that was used to minimize windows. A similar concept to the Windows taskbar appeared even earlier in 1988, in the NeXTSTEP operating system for Steve Jobs’s NeXT computers, so many assumed the inspiration came from there. However, according to Microsoft veterans, this wasn’t the case. (The NeXTSTEP solution actually went on to become the direct precursor to macOS’s Dock.) Over the years, the taskbar in Windows has evolved quite a bit. However, the most criticized change occurred in 2021 with the advent of Windows 11, which fixed the taskbar to the center of the bottom edge and removed the ability to reposition it. Users hated the lack of customization so much that Microsoft recently brought that taskbar feature back.

item.title: Firefox 155 patches 30 security flaws, adds sortable tab groups
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Score: 5.25
The newest major release of Firefox 155 for Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android brings a number of improvements, including support for Nintendo Switch Pro controllers and sortable tab groups. Mozilla has also patched over 30 security vulnerabilities, and updates are also available for the ESR versions of Firefox for older systems. The release of the next major version, Firefox 156, is already scheduled for September 15th, with time for a bug-fix update on September 8th. What’s new in Firefox 155? The “AI” feature known as “Smart Window” (currently still labeled as a beta version) now makes it easier to revisit topics you’ve already covered. Questions are intended to be answered more quickly, complete with source references. It’s being rolled out gradually. The isolated tab environments introduced with Firefox 153 can now be sorted according to user preferences in settings. Tab environments isolate cookies from one another, allowing you to log in to the same website with different accounts across different tabs. This means you can, for example, actively use multiple Gmail inboxes at once. Another small improvement involves the display in the address bar that shows how many trackers were blocked on the current page. Firefox now allows this display to be disabled in the settings without turning off tracker blocking altogether. This feature is being rolled out gradually. The free built-in VPN feature, which was introduced back in Firefox 149, continues to offer the expanded selection of 32 virtual locations, but now that August is over, the unlimited data usage has been ended and is now capped at 50GB per month again. The free VPN is now also rolling out on Firefox for Android, with iOS set to follow soon. Other improvements include: the ability to scale up small PDF files to fit paper size when printing, and support for Nintendo Switch Pro controllers when playing browser-based online games on Windows. Since Firefox 154, there’s also been support for game streaming with Nvidia GeForce Now. Security flaws fixed in Firefox 155 In the security advisory for Firefox 155, Mozilla lists 29 security vulnerabilities that have been fixed, 25 of which were discovered and reported by external security researchers. Mozilla classifies 10 of these vulnerabilities as high risk, including several use-after-free (UAF) flaws that could allow malicious code to escape the browser’s sandbox. The last four entries in the security advisory (CVE-2026-84142 to CVE-2026-84145) summarize an unspecified number of internally discovered security flaws—most of which are classified as high risk—resulting from programming errors in memory management. The vulnerabilities are grouped according to which program versions are affected. Tip: Whether you keep your browser up to date, you need proper antivirus protections if you want your PC to remain secure and private. Check out our picks for the best antivirus software for Windows as well as best VPN services to stay ahead of security problems. Firefox ESR browser updates Alongside Firefox 155.0, the ESR versions 153.2.0, 140.15.0, and 115.40.0 are also available. The latter is only available for Windows 7 and 8.1, and macOS 10.12 to 10.14, and will remain so at least until March 2027. In the ESR versions, Mozilla has fixed the above-mentioned vulnerabilities that were also present in the code of those previous browser generations. This amounts to more than 24 vulnerabilities fixed in Firefox 153.2.0, at least 11 in Firefox 140.15, and at least six in Firefox 115.40. Firefox ESR 140 will receive a final update to version 140.17 at the end of September. This generation will then be replaced by Firefox ESR 153.

item.title: This Windows security trick auto-locks your PC when you leave
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Score: 5.02
I’m pretty good about remembering to lock my PC when I leave my desk, but every once in a while I forget. Thankfully, when I walk away from my computer and my brain is already halfway to the coffee machine, there’s an easy way to keep it protected. Windows’ Dynamic Lock gives you a handy backup plan by using your phone to tell when you’ve walked away. Joel Lee / IDG Dynamic Lock works via Bluetooth. Pair your phone with your Windows PC, then go to Settings > Accounts > Sign-in options > Dynamic lock and enable the option that lets Windows lock your device when you’re away. Once it’s turned on, Windows monitors the Bluetooth signal from your phone. When you walk far enough away that the signal drops out of range, Windows assumes you’ve left and automatically locks your PC. Microsoft says this should happen within about a minute after your phone goes out of Bluetooth range. In my experience, it usually takes less than 30 seconds. Dynamic Lock is really handy at an office, coffee shop, library, or anywhere else you might step away from your computer and need to secure it. While Dynamic Lock is a useful backup, it shouldn’t be treated as a replacement for directly locking your computer with Win + L. Dynamic Lock isn’t instant. There can be a short window between you leaving and Windows locking itself, and Bluetooth isn’t something I’d want to depend on as my only line of defense. When you can, always try to remember to press Win + L before leaving your PC. For more fun and helpful tips, tricks, and website and app recommendations, be sure to subscribe to our PCWorld Try This newsletter.

item.title: Windows could lock you out of your PC. Save your recovery key now!
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Score: 4.70
In the Pro editions of Windows, the BitLocker hard drive encryption feature has been included since Windows Vista. Under the name Device Encryption, it also became part of the Home editions with Windows 10, and since Windows 11 24H2 it has even been enabled by default. This is problematic because not all users are aware of this, and the system may suddenly demand the recovery key — for example, following a UEFI update. However, without this 48-digit code, you will no longer have any access to your data on the hard drive! You will then be locked out, regardless of whether you try to boot the computer from the hard drive or via an alternative system from an external storage device. To ensure that this worst-case scenario does not happen to you under any circumstances, you should make sure to back up the recovery key in good time. This is particularly important if you’re using device encryption on a computer with a local user account! If you’re signed in with a Microsoft account, you can still retrieve the code via that account at a later date. Here’s how: In the Home editions of Windows 10 and 11, the hard drive may be encrypted even if you haven’t enabled the feature yourself. Foundry Specifically, this happens whenever you use a Microsoft account as intended during the initial setup. You can check this by clicking on ‘Privacy and security > Device encryption’ in the Settings app. If the ‘Device encryption’ option is enabled, open the address https://aka.ms/myrecoverykey in your browser and sign in with your Microsoft account. Now make a note of the key ID and the recovery key. This will allow you to access the code later on another computer. Tip: If you use different computers with the same Microsoft account, or have done so in the past, all of these devices will appear in the online list. This makes it more difficult to find the correct key; in some cases, the only solution is to try them out one by one! Please note that the individual partitions are encrypted separately and therefore require different recovery keys to decrypt them. The abbreviation OSV (Operating System Volume) refers to the system drive, while FDV (Fixed Data Volume) refers to other data drives. It becomes risky if you are suddenly asked for the recovery key without a Microsoft account. First, without an online account, there is no automatic backup. Second, the Home Edition of Windows offers no obvious option for saving the key: The ability to print it out or transfer it to a USB stick, as is possible with BitLocker in the Pro version, is missing here. Furthermore, users of local accounts are effectively misled when enabling device encryption. This is because the system then suggests, in a message highlighted in yellow, that an online account is required to encrypt the hard drive. But that’s not true; in fact, encryption starts automatically in the background as soon as the device is switched on! You can see this by launching the Command Prompt (cmd) with administrator rights, typing the command manage-bde.exe -status C: and pressing the Enter key. Do not be lulled into a false sense of security by the entry under ‘Protection status’, which suggests that (hard drive) protection is disabled — this is definitely incorrect. It is therefore absolutely vital to back up the key you are using in case you ever need it to decrypt the volume and regain access to your stored data. To save it, type the command manage-bde.exe -protectors -get C: into the open Command Prompt and press the Enter key again. The 48-character key — referred to here as the ‘password’ — will then appear below the ID mentioned earlier. Select this with the mouse, copy it to the clipboard, and then print it out and/or save it to a USB stick. Please keep the printout and the USB stick in a secure yet easy-to-remember place.

item.title: Windows 11’s decluttered right-click menu draws criticism for one big flaw
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Score: 4.30
In summary: - PCWorld reports that Windows 11’s upcoming 26H2 update, expected this October, introduces a redesigned right-click menu called the Split Context Menu, aimed at reducing clutter. - The new SplitMenuFlyoutItem feature groups context-aware options more cleanly, but users may lose quick access to custom registry shortcuts, which could be pushed into submenus. - Critics argue the cleaner menu comes at the cost of flexibility, making it more restrictive for power users. Updated on September 1st, 2026: Microsoft is finally streamlining the Windows 11 right-click menu with the upcoming 26H2 update in October. However, some Insiders with preview access have criticized Microsoft’s implementation and its limitations. The main complaint comes from users who have added their own context menu entries via the Windows Registry. Those entries will be shown under the “Show more options” submenu, which must be activated manually in the Settings. In other words, accessing these entries will become more cumbersome than it is now pre-update. (Currently, these custom entries appear as top-level actions in the context menu.) In short, if you want to benefit from the streamlined context menu design, you essentially have to give up on custom entries and the “Show more options” submenu. It’s unclear whether Microsoft will take this criticism aboard and make changes prior to 26H2’s release. Original story from November 6th, 2025: The Context Menu in Windows 11 (also known as the right-click menu) is meant to be a convenient shortcut for common actions, making it much easier to do various things via just a few simple clicks. But over time, the Windows 11 Context Menu has grown cluttered and unusable. Microsoft isn’t just aware of this, but also committed to rectifying it. In a WinUI Community Call video stream that went live yesterday, one section covered improvements to the Context Menu that are currently being explored. The revamp is being called Split Context Menu. In Microsoft’s own words, the current MenuFlyoutItem control doesn’t allow for split actions, which is why the menu has grown so cluttered over the years. Furthermore, the Windows 11 Context Menu is—despite its name—not truly contextual, meaning it includes way too many items even in contexts where some of those items don’t make sense. The solution? A new control called SplitMenuFlyoutItem, which will support “context-aware groupings and customizations” that allow the Context Menu to adapt to user selections. WinUI developers will be able to define primary and secondary actions, paving the way for submenus that improve workflows and reduce main menu clutter. As of now, it’s unclear when the new Split Context Menu will be made available to the public. The API will first need to be developed, then presumably it will need to be tested by Windows Insiders.

item.title: pCloud online backup review: A lifetime of secure files at a bargain price
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Score: 3.96
At a glance Expert's Rating Pros - Online storage, multi-device sync, and mirroring - Fantastically affordable lifetime plans - Extremely secure and private - Free 6GB account Cons - Interface and operational quirks - Document editing is weak - Two-way sync only Our Verdict Though the initial cost might throw off some users, pCloud’s yearly and lifetime plans are affordable in the long run and the service offers several ways to store and sync data via its versatile client software. Price When Reviewed This value will show the geolocated pricing text for product undefined Best Pricing Today Price When Reviewed Annual: $59.88 (currently $49.99) for 500GB for a year; $119.88 (currently $99.99) for 2TB; Lifetime: $299 (currently $199) for 500GB; or $599 (currently $399) for 2TB; $1,890 (currently $1,190) 10TB Best Prices Today: pCloud greatly resembles services like Dropbox and OneDrive in its implementation, with Windows Explorer integration and full web-browser functionality. That said, it’s also a bit easier to get up to speed with than those others. pCloud is also touted as uber-secure. I even like its lifetime pricing, as opposed to the usual monthly rate. Let’s cover that first. Read on to learn more, then see our roundup of the best online backup for comparison. How much does pCloud cost? After our original review, pCloud added yearly rates to their lifetime plans which are less likely to daunt new buyers: $50 for 500GB, $100 for 2TB, and $200 for 10TB. Not amazing bargains, but competitive. The single-user lifetime plans, if you don’t do the division, might seem daunting at first: $199 for 500GB, $399 for 2TB, and $1,190 for 10TB. Note that those are discounts from the standard rates of $300, $600, and $1,890 at the time of this writing. However, if you break down those discounted prices over, say, a mere five years, it’s roughly $80 per terabyte per year for the 500GB plan, $40 per TB per year for the 2TB option, and approximately $24 per TB per year annually for the 10TB/$1,190 tier. Not bad, and of course, the longer you go, the cheaper it gets. If you opt for a lifetime plan, you must believe that the company will remain in business. There’s no way for us to guarantee any company’s survival, but pCloud has been around for 12 years and is based in Switzerland — a country with a long history of safe-guarding valuables. pCloud also explained that it has a refund policy in place, as well as contingency plans for a force majeure. Happily, there’s also a free 10GB plan so you can try pCloud without risk. What are pCloud’s features? pCloud’s primary feature is, of course, its online storage. To upload and sync your data, the company provides clients for Android, iOS, Windows, and macOS, as well as a very well thought-out and capable web interface with some neat tricks up its sleeve. pCloud is unique in my experience by virtue of providing access to your online files via a virtual drive (pDrive with the drive letter P: — get it?!) rather than the dedicated-folder metaphor that Dropbox, Google and others use. The Windows and macOS clients let you sync any folder you wish to your online storage, and cleverly/automatically create a suitable folder name for the online half (assuming you need a new folder). pCloud sync is two-way, so the standard caveat applies — you need to be careful about what you delete online as that will be reflected in the local folder. Files dragged to the P: drive exist both in that drive locally and online, but aren’t mirrored, i.e. changes aren’t reflected. Sync files are mirrored, and files backed up with the client software exist only in their original location and online. My only real problem with pCloud was that when I reinstalled it for my latest look, it automatically started downloading files to the P: drive without asking. After a complete uninstall, which entailed finding and deleting the sync folder manually, it then decided to ask. pCloud could be a bit smarter about that. One of my favorite pCloud tricks is backing up the data from other online storage services. It’s not as comprehensive in that regard as Arq 7, but the list will cover most end users: Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox and Dropbox Business, Google Photos, Instagram, and Facebook. The first four are manually invoked operations, while the last three are ongoing. You must sign in to the services for pCloud to back them up as per usual. Note that the online storage backups are true backup, not sync. The pCloud Windows client has a backup tab, but it’s misleading as I’ll discuss in depth below. Another useful pCloud feature is the Crypto folder. This is a folder with a secondary password for even stronger protection. If there’s stuff you really don’t want anyone to see, this will interest you. Not that people are likely to stumble on to your non-crypto data if you use a suitably strong primary password. Other functions include file sharing and file requests (i.e., let someone ask and upload something to your account). pCloud offers several ancillary services including: the pCloud Transfer file-transfer portal, which works with files up to 5GB; and the pCloud Save extension for browsers. The latter is supposed to save images and other files to a pCloud Save folder, but I had only moderate success with it. Finally, there’s pCloud Password, a password manager service. pCloud allows you to view many types of files, but it’s hardly the equal of say OneDrive or Google Drive in that regard. In my tests, the pCloud viewing was fine with photos, decent with Word files and PDFs, but Excel files were displayed as one column per page. Trying to view an MP4 video stalled as well. Editing of files is available, but it’s rudimentary, of the overlay type normally associated with images. If you want granular word processing, PDF, spreadsheet, etc. editing, Google Drive or OneDrive might suit you better. Another thing I was a bit annoyed with was the feedback at the bottom of the program window: It tells you something’s happening, but it’s not specific enough. Is it for sync, or backup? I’d like to know. Caveat about the Windows client’s ‘Backup’ function Before I tried it, I was going to bestow upon pCloud major kudos for including a discrete Windows backup function. However, it’s not backup, it’s two-way sync of pre-selected (documents, pictures, etc.) and user-selected folders where changes at either end are duplicated at the other. This is, however, somewhat mitigated by 15 to 180 day retention of revisions and deleted files, which are available in the recently implemented Rewind function (shown below) when you access a backup via the web portal. Unlike Backblaze thfere is no option for permanent retention, but you can extend the period. As pCloud’s backups of your phone and online services are true immutable backups, the company is obviously aware of the difference. Your guess is as good as mine as to the reason for this vocabulary faux pas, but it came darn close to costing an otherwise excellent service half a star. How fast is pCloud? In uploading around 100GB of data, I had no issues with pCloud. It didn’t slow down my system, and the backup proceeded largely in line with the speed of my 2.5Gbps network and 7.5MBps/2.5MBps download/upload speed of local Bay Area broadband provider Monkeybrains. Should you buy pCloud? pCloud might appear expensive at first glance, but it’s actually very affordable if you plan to back up your data online for any significant period of time. The unique features are also quite handy, so for the most part, color me impressed and consider the answer to this question yes. At the very least, sign up for the free incarnation. Who couldn’t use 10GB of free storage to mirror one or more of your other online data repositories? Just remember that the Window’s client’s backup function is actually sync. This article was edited on May 1, 2026 for clarity and additional info, then again on August 1 to add more information and more recent images. Editor’s note: Because online services are often iterative, gaining new features and performance improvements over time, this review is subject to change in order to accurately reflect the current state of the service. Any changes to text will be noted above this notice and changed conclusions at the top.

item.title: Geekom mini-PC owners may need to nuke Windows and start over
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Score: 3.69
In summary: - PCWorld reports that Geekom mini-PC owners may have unknowingly installed malware-laced network drivers hosted on the company’s legacy support pages. - Affected models include the A7, A8, AE7, AE8, AX7 Pro, and AX8 Pro, with risks including redirected internet traffic, app interference, and hackers gaining backdoor access. - Users with infected devices are advised to perform a clean Windows reinstall, and should rely on Windows Update or trusted vendor sites like Realtek for drivers. You’re a conscientious computer owner. You download and install the latest network driver for your machine. If you own a Geekom mini-PC, you may now need to completely wipe Windows and start all over. The issue: A legacy support webpage served malware-laced network drivers for Geekom’s A7, A8, AE7, AE8, AX7 Pro and AX8 Pro models. While Geekom no longer linked to it within its own site, the page was still indexed by search engines—leading people directly to the bad software. As verified by Videocardz.com, installing the tainted drivers allowed hackers to place a backdoor on affected PCs, spy on activity, redirect internet traffic, and interfere with normal operation of Windows apps. The issue was initially identified by Reddit users as early as December 2024. Following Videocardz.com’s initial report, Geekom pulled down the problematic legacy page. (No word still on how the malware ended up in an official software download.) However, if you believe your PC is affected, you should take immediate steps to secure your PC. With this type of malware on your system, someone could steal information from your computer while maintaining persistent access to it, too. The fix: Back up your documents and files, then perform a clean install of Windows. (Completely nuke everything, then reinstall Windows.) Because of the malware type, you want to start over from scratch. PCWorld In general, the smart move is to get drivers through Windows first. If that doesn’t work, look up the manufacturer of the hardware component, then head to that vendor’s site. (You can usually find this information on your device’s official specifications page.) For the Geekom mini-PCs, the Realtek website has the necessary network driver. The other takeaway? Googling for a support page isn’t always safe—at least, not when you’re dealing with smaller companies. They may not maintain or invest in software verification, especially for legacy pages.

item.title: Nvidia is cutting Windows 10 gamers down to security patches only
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Score: 3.68
In summary: - PCWorld reports that Nvidia will stop releasing new feature and performance updates for Windows 10 Game Ready Drivers after October 2026, shifting to quarterly security fixes only. - This means Windows 10 gamers may experience bugs or poor optimization in newer game titles lacking critical driver updates. - Full GeForce driver support ends completely by November 2029, making an upgrade to Windows 11 the recommended move for gamers. Even though Microsoft is providing security updates for Windows 10 until October 2027 via the Extended Security Updates (ESU) program, graphics card giant Nvidia is pulling out before then. Apart from security updates, Nvidia is ending Windows 10 feature support—a major blow for gamers still on the much-beloved operating system. According to this support page (spotted by Windows Latest), Nvidia says: “After October 2026, Windows 10 driver support will transition to a quarterly security update for a period of three years where critical bug fixes will be delivered to end users through October 2029.” Practically speaking, this means Nvidia will no longer release performance updates and new features for its “Game Ready Drivers” and “Nvidia Studio Drivers” on Windows 10. In short, Windows 10 users who have GeForce graphics cards in their PCs will be left hanging in the cold soon. Nvidia is one of the first major companies to drop Windows 10 support. At first, the company went along with Microsoft’s decision to extend support for Windows 10 by one year (from October 2025 to October 2026). However, Nvidia isn’t re-upping on that decision with Microsoft’s second extension. GeForce drivers on Windows 10 will only get security updates once every quarter between October 2026 and October 2029. Starting November 2029, GeForce drivers on Windows 10 will no longer receive any updates of any kind. Existing games will continue to work on Windows 10 PCs. However, if new bugs are discovered in them, Nvidia will no longer provide bug fixes or optimizations. This drawback is likely to grow more noticeable over time. Furthermore, Windows 10 users will not receive optimizations for newly released games. This could mean that gamers on Windows 10 PCs are left to deal with performance issues or bugs in new game titles on their own. This, in turn, is likely to lead to more gamers switching to Windows 11.

item.title: Get Cooler Master’s crazy sneaker PC case, plus an AIO and PSU, for just $240
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Score: 3.05
Small form factor PC builds are often a bit on the low-key side — usually a tiny, unobtrusive box full of parts. But Cooler Master’s sneaker case is the exception to that rule, a showpiece meant more to be looked at than played on. After debuting at trade shows it went for $3500 as a pre-built, but now you can score the case for just $240. This is most decidedly not a full pre-built desktop, so you’ll have to supply some of the desktop parts yourself. It comes with a 360mm liquid cooler for the CPU and a respectable 850-watt power supply. That means you’re on the hook for a Mini-ITX motherboard, processor, RAM, storage, and GPU, the latter of which can’t be more than 304mm long and 61mm tall. That’s going to be a pretty big bill to fill out a desktop build, but even with today’s insane prices, you can put one together for far less than the original price of the pre-built desktop. That said, I can’t imagine that it’ll be as easy as building in a regular case, even a SFF one. A fun project to be sure, but probably not a great idea for a first-time builder. If you’re up to the challenge, Woot is selling the case for the next three days. Or until the stock sells out…which is very possible, since I can’t imagine there are many of these still available at any price.

item.title: Beatbot AquaSense 2 Ultra review: Excellent navigation comes at a price
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Score: 2.38
At a glance Expert's Rating Pros - AI finds and cleans leftover leaves - Climbs above the waterline - Parks at the pool edge and sends an alert - Lots of useful accessories Cons - Heavy - No fine filter for pollen Our Verdict Overall, the AquaSense 2 Ultra is a great choice for larger, more demanding pools, but its high price is hard to justify for a standard pool. Price at time of review This value will show the geolocated pricing text for product undefined Best Price Today Price When Reviewed $3,550.00 Best Prices Today: Beatbot AquaSense 2 Ultra Battery-powered pool robots now use structured navigation, route planning, wall detection, and app connectivity, with software becoming an increasingly important differentiator. Beatbot positions itself at the forefront in this area with the AquaSense 2 Ultra. In a practical test carried out in a round foil above-ground pool with a stainless steel ladder, the setup, app control, standard cleaning cycle, and post-cleaning procedures were assessed. Christoph Hoffmann Beatbot AquaSense 2 Ultra: Design and build quality Beatbot positions the AquaSense 2 Ultra as the flagship model of the AquaSense series, and it certainly looks the part. The housing measures 17.9 × 17.3 × 10.9 inches and weighs 29.1 pounds when empty. This makes the AquaSense 2 Ultra one of the heavier pool robots. The Mova Rover X10 weighs in at 34.8 pounds, while the Mammotion Spino E1 weighs just 20.5 pounds. The difference is even more striking when compared to the Aiper Scuba V3, which, at around 18.1 pounds, weighs about 11 pounds or less. This difference is clearly noticeable when lifting the robot over the side of an above-ground pool, as the weight of the remaining water is temporarily added until it has drained out through the SmartDrain openings. Christoph Hoffmann The surface features a dark blue IMR coating, which is applied via injection molding and, according to the manufacturer, protects against UV radiation and mechanical abrasion. It looks high-quality, but shows every water droplet and fingerprint. The handle on the top is deep enough to fit the whole hand. Given the weight, this is no minor detail. Christoph Hoffmann The front is striking. Behind a viewing window sits the HybridSense module with a camera and two LEDs for additional lighting. Above it, two small side brushes rotate, designed to guide floating debris towards the suction inlet. On the underside, wide rubber tracks work in conjunction with two light-grey roller brushes. The tracks have a coarse tread and provide reliable grip on smooth pool liners. Christoph Hoffmann The build quality is excellent. The gaps are even, and the large flap closes securely. Nothing rattles during operation, either. The robot is IP68-rated and designed for underwater operation. The charging dock, on the other hand, is only IPX4-rated and should be kept in a covered, dry place. The app explicitly points this out during charging. Beatbot AquaSense 2 Ultra: Specifications, filtration According to the manufacturer, the device uses a quad-core CPU, 11 motors and sensors comprising an AI camera, two TOF and two infrared sensors, and four ultrasonic sensors. The official battery life figures range from 10 to 11 hours on the surface and five to six hours on the seabed. The battery has a capacity of 13,400 mAh and charges wirelessly via the vertical charging cradle. Beatbot states that a full charge takes 4.5 hours. The circulation rate is up to 5,500 US GPH. The Spino E1 manages around 5,800 GPH, while the Rover X10 manages up to 10,000 GPH. The Beatbot’s advantage lies not in its pump flow rate, but in its navigation. Filtration is carried out via two nested baskets with volumes of four and 3.9 quarts. The finest mesh is rated at 150 microns. This is sufficient for leaves, insects, coarse sand, and small pebbles, while very fine suspended particles and pollen may sometimes pass through. Christoph Hoffmann In this respect, the significantly cheaper Aiper Scuba V3 is better equipped. In addition to its 180-micron coarse filter, a replaceable 3-micron MicroMesh membrane is included. In our test, it even retained pollen and very fine suspended particles. However, the fine membrane clogs up quickly in heavily contaminated water and requires a powerful jet of water to rinse clean. With the Beatbot, a finer double filter basket has to be purchased separately. The ClearWater technology is designed to close this gap, at least in part. In a separate chamber beneath the flap sits a blue cartridge containing a chitosan-based clarifying agent derived from crab shells. Chitosan acts as a flocculant and can aggregate very small suspended solids into larger particle clusters. Whether these subsequently actually end up in the robot’s 150-micron filter depends, among other things, on the dosage, water chemistry, circulation, and particle type. The process does not replace true fine filtration. Compared with Aiper’s 3-micron membranes, the Beatbot remains at a design disadvantage. Christoph Hoffmann One cartridge holds 300 milliliters and is sufficient for four treatments. Replacement cartridges are on offer from around $220 for 12 cartridges, which are intended to last six months. Once opened, the clarifying agent should be used up within 30 days. Dosing is triggered either via the switch in the app or by pressing and holding the button on the base of the device for three seconds. A purple light confirms the process. The user resets the consumption counter themselves. This is an inelegant solution, as the app does not know the actual fill level. There are four programs to choose from. Floor mode cleans only the base of the pool. Standard mode adds the walls and waterline. Pro mode includes the surface as well. There is also a custom mode, in which the number of passes per zone can be set individually, including a zone mode for pools with multiple levels. Once synchronised, the settings configured in the app can be started using the fifth button on the robot. Beatbot AquaSense 2 Ultra: Setup Some manual work is required before first use. The two side brushes are supplied as loose rubber strips and must be stretched around the brush wheels and secured. The charging cradle also only becomes stable once two stand feet have been inserted. Most competitors come fully assembled out of the box. Christoph Hoffmann The rest is quick. After creating an account in the Beatbot app, you scan the QR code on the robot. In our test, the device registered within a few seconds, displaying its model name and serial number, followed by Wi-Fi pairing. The robot supports 2.4 and 5 GHz as well as Bluetooth. A second attempt wasn’t necessary. Christoph Hoffmann Immediately after pairing, the app offered a firmware update from version 0.0.92 to 0.1.23 – a whopping 84.54 MB. It completed without any interruptions. It is worth noting that automatic updates are disabled by default. Without automatic updates enabled, firmware updates can be easily overlooked. I’d recommend enabling automatic updates immediately after setup. Christoph Hoffmann The most interesting features have been moved to the Lab Features section. These include visual AI recognition, the auxiliary light for poor visibility, and smart parking in shallow water. AI recognition and the auxiliary light are active, but smart parking is not. Christoph Hoffmann Beatbot AquaSense 2 Ultra: Performance The test was carried out in a round above-ground pool with a smooth liner and a suspended stainless-steel ladder. Round pools make it difficult to plan a consistent cleaning path, as there are no long, straight edges to use for orientation. Christoph Hoffmann The procedure is simple. After switching it on and selecting the mode, the robot is placed in the water. The device fills its chambers with water, rotates once on the surface to orientate itself, then sinks to the bottom. In standard mode, it first cleans the floor in parallel paths, then it climbs up the wall and cleans the waterline. Christoph Hoffmann Stubborn lines of grime had built up on the pool floor over several years. The AquaSense 2 Ultra was able to remove most of it. The robot really comes into its own on the wall. The chains grip securely on the smooth liner, and it climbs without slipping. At the waterline, the body extends a few inches above the water’s surface and remains there. The robot also removed the typical build-up of sun cream and skin oils at the waterline. According to the manufacturer, the robot passes over the waterline twice per cycle. The AquaSense 2 Ultra navigated the suspended ladder without any intervention. It approached, stopped, reversed, and maneuvered round the rungs. It did not get stuck under the steps. It was precisely this type of ladder that the Aiper Scuba V3 struggled with. It became wedged under the rungs on several occasions and, at times, allowed its chains to run over the liner for 20 to 30 seconds before reversing. In this regard, the Beatbot’s obstacle detection is noticeably more reliable. Christoph Hoffmann After the regular floor clean, the robot switches to AI-assisted dirt detection. It first moves through the pool without any discernible pattern until the camera detects dirt. It then corrects course, drives over the spot, stops, and repeats the movement forwards and backwards. This movement pattern did indeed result in targeted spot cleaning. The Beatbot goes a step further in its use of the camera than the Aiper does with the Scuba V3. The latter’s AI camera is primarily used for navigation, obstacle detection, and adaptive route planning. The AquaSense 2 Ultra also uses the camera for targeted dirt detection. After its regular cycle, it searches for any remaining dirt and returns to the areas it has detected. This difference was evident during direct testing. Christoph Hoffmann Of the ten test leaves added to the water afterward, the robot picked up nine. After 85 minutes, no visible patches of dirt remained in the test tank. The filter basket contained sand, fine plant matter, and leaves. Surface cleaning, however, is significantly less effective. As it moves, the robot pushes a bow wave in front of it, which pushes floating leaves to the side rather than directing them into the suction opening. The new side brushes mitigate the effect, but do not eliminate it. Anyone wishing to keep the water’s surface reliably clear will have no choice but to use a dedicated skimmer or landing net. Consequently, the advertised surface cleaning remains the weakest of the five areas of application. Christoph Hoffmann A second weakness concerns connectivity. As soon as the robot submerges, the app connection is lost. Status checks and mode changes are only possible again once the device is floating on the surface. Physically, this is understandable, as water strongly attenuates radio waves. However, this problem is not unique to the Beatbot. The connection to the Aiper Scuba V3 also dropped after it submerged. Battery level and completion notifications were only reliably available again once it had resurfaced. Neither of the two AI pool robots offers continuous communication while underwater. Mova solves this in the Rover X10 using a more technically complex solution: a floating buoy that receives Wi-Fi commands and relays them to the robot via ultrasound. Given the high price, this limitation is particularly significant. Consequently, the remote control mentioned in the data sheet also only works at the surface. At the end of the cycle, the robot first moves to the edge of the pool and waits there at the water’s edge. If it is not retrieved, it later breaks away from the edge and floats freely on the surface. It can be recalled using the Park button in the app. Lifting it out remains the most tedious part of daily use. When lifting it over the wall of an above-ground pool, the 29.1 pounds plus residual water are clearly noticeable. The retrieval hook is included but is rarely needed if the Park function is working properly. Once the cycle is complete, the app notifies you via a push notification and prompts you to clean the filter basket immediately. The log showed 258 square feet over a running time of 85 minutes. Extrapolated to a full load, this works out to a little over four hours Standard mode. The manufacturer’s specification of five hours refers to bottom-cleaning operation only and is therefore plausible. Christoph Hoffmann The schematic map shows the basic layout and paths taken. However, it does not allow for targeted planning, as restricted zones and individual areas are missing. In custom mode, surfaces, floors, and walls can each be combined with up to two passes. The selected configuration is then synchronized with the robot. Christoph Hoffmann The filter basket is removed from the top. The blue clip is secure, and the basket can be removed with one hand. It can be rinsed clean using a garden hose. Because the basket does not open downward, a fair amount of water pressure is needed to dislodge sand stuck in the corners. The Rover X10 exhibited the same shortcoming. Christoph Hoffmann The robot is clearly audible on the surface. Underwater, however, it’s barely noticeable. Beatbot AquaSense 2 Ultra: Conclusion The AquaSense 2 Ultra performs very well at the core tasks expected of a pool robot. The floor, walls, and waterline remain clean, and the navigation system is easy to follow. The camera-based post-cleaning check proved to be a tangible benefit in the test. In backyards with trees, it noticeably reduces the need for a pool net. Surface cleaning falls short of expectations, and the standard fine filtration stops at 150 microns. Aipet offers a significantly finer filter with its 3-micron membrane. Added to this are the lack of app connectivity underwater and the ongoing costs of the clarifying agent. That leaves the price. At around $3,150, the AquaSense 2 Ultra costs roughly three times as much as an Aiper Scuba V3, which is available for around $1,050. Yet the Aiper also cleans the floor, walls, and waterline, navigates using a camera and, once the work is done, parks at the edge of the pool for removal. It even has advantages in terms of weight and standard fine filtration: weighing 18.1 pounds, it’s considerably lighter, and a 3-micron membrane is already included in the box. The Beatbot stands out in terms of obstacle detection, targeted AI dirt detection, and additional surface and platform cleaning. Whether these features justify the premium price depends heavily on the pool and the level of dirt. The AquaSense 2 Ultra really comes into its own in large or irregularly shaped pools with sunbathing areas and a high volume of fallen leaves. For a standard round pool, however, its range of features is harder to justify. Beatbot AquaSense 2 Ultra: Technical specifications - Model: Beatbot AquaSense 2 Ultra - Type: Cordless, rechargeable pool robot with AI camera - Cleaning areas: Floor, walls, waterline, surface, platforms from a water depth of 35 cm - Navigation: HybridSense AI pool mapping, CleverNav - Sensors: AI camera, two TOF, two infrared sensors, four ultrasonic sensors - Processor: Quad-core CPU - Motors: 11 - Propulsion: Rubber tracks, six guide wheels, and two drive wheels - Brushes: Two side brushes, two roller brushes - Circulation capacity: Up to 5,500 GPH, approx. 20,800 l/h - Filter: Double basket, 4.0 and 3.7 liters, finest mesh size 150 - Water clarification: ClearWater with chitosan clarifying agent, 300 ml per cartridge, four applications - Battery: 13,400 mAh, up to 10 hours on the surface, up to five hours on the bottom, up to 4.5 hours on the walls and waterline - Charging time: 4.5 hours, wireless charging cradle - Coverage: Up to 320 m² per charge - Operating depth: 0.4 to 3.0 metres - Cleaning modes: Floor, Standard, Pro, Custom (including Area Mode) - Surfaces: Vinyl, concrete, fibreglass, ceramic tiles, stainless steel, mosaic - Salt water: Suitable for up to 5 g/l - Connectivity: Wi-Fi 2.4 and 5 GHz, Bluetooth - Controls: Buttons on the unit, Beatbot app, remote control on the surface - Protection rating: IP68 (robot), IPX4 (charging dock) - Dimensions: 454 × 439 × 278 mm - Weight: 21.1 pounds - Contents: Robot, charging cradle with power adaptor, clarifying agent cartridge, protective cover, retrieval hook, two side brush strips, screws, screwdriver, quick start guide - Warranty: 3 years with full replacement - Updates: OTA firmware updates

item.title: OpenAI's Astra model is cleared for release after hitting its highest cybersecurity risk threshold
item.description:
Source: Quartz Score: 6.18
OpenAI said Tuesday it plans to release its Astra model after determining that new safeguards are sufficient to manage the risks posed by the system, which the company has designated as meeting its highest cybersecurity capability threshold. The company said Astra is the first model it has designated "Critical" under its Preparedness Framework, capable of finding and exploiting unknown security flaws without human guidance Astra is the first model OpenAI has rated "Critical" under its Preparedness Framework, a designation reflecting the company's assessment that the system can independently identify novel security vulnerabilities and craft exploits against hardened targets without requiring human direction at each step. The company said it believes Astra's safeguards "sufficiently minimize the risk of severe harm for release" under that framework, but did not provide a specific release date. Access to Astra's most advanced cybersecurity features will be restricted at launch. A small group of testers will receive initial access, with broader availability through OpenAI's Daybreak Blue cybersecurity program to follow. In internal testing, Astra scored 100% on ExploitBench, a benchmark measuring a model's ability to develop exploits from known vulnerabilities. On a separate internal benchmark covering 20 high-severity vulnerabilities disclosed between June and August 2026, the model discovered and used two zero-day vulnerabilities as part of an exploit chain. OpenAI said it is disclosing those vulnerabilities to the relevant maintainers. Expert-led assessments found that Astra built a full browser-compromise chain that escaped a sandbox and executed commands on a host machine. It also combined multiple vulnerabilities in a hardened operating system into a privilege-escalation chain from an unprivileged user to root. OpenAI said Astra refused 91.5% of requests in cyber jailbreak evaluations, compared with 59% for its predecessor GPT-5.6 Sol, citing new training techniques for model robustness. OpenAI said it has identified two distinct risk scenarios it is working to guard against: deliberate misuse by bad actors seeking to launch attacks, and the possibility of the model acting on its own to conduct unauthorized operations. To guard against the latter, the company said it is implementing chain-of-thought monitoring systems capable of identifying and interrupting actions that fall outside authorized boundaries. The company acknowledged that the safeguards may mistakenly flag legitimate activity, which could slow, pause, or stop tasks unrelated to cybersecurity. OpenAI paused parts of Astra's development last month after preliminary evaluations suggested the model might reach the Critical threshold. The company also halted some frontier training runs following a separate incident in which earlier unreleased OpenAI models broke out of their controlled environment and compromised AI platform Hugging Face's systems. OpenAI said Astra was not involved in that incident, but incorporated lessons from it into Astra's safeguards, including stronger refusal training and additional misuse protections. OpenAI VP of research Amelia Glaese said in a briefing Tuesday that the company had invested in stronger model-layer protections for Astra than for any prior release, according to Axios. OpenAI researcher Fouad Matin said the company believes Astra's cybersecurity capabilities can help defenders find and fix vulnerabilities, but that without appropriate safeguards, the same capabilities could benefit attackers, according to Axios. item.title: The global bond selloff is getting worse
item.description:
Source: Quartz Score: 5.67
A global government bond selloff intensified on Tuesday, pushing yields across major economies to their highest levels in years as renewed U.S.-Iran tensions drove oil prices higher and fanned inflation fears. The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield advanced 3 basis points, settling at 4.788% — a level not reached since Jan. 14, 2025. The 30-year Treasury yield ended the session at 5.272%, a gain of more than 2 basis points, and the 2-year note moved up by more than 1 basis point to reach 4.362%. One basis point equals 0.01%. Bond markets beyond the U.S. also came under pressure. The 10-year Japanese government bond yield crossed 3% for the first time since 1996, according to The New York Times. The 10-year German Bund yield reached 3.364%, a level last seen in 2011, according to The Wall Street Journal. U.K. gilt yields also climbed sharply, with the 10-year reaching 5.254% — a level not touched since 2008 — and the 30-year hitting its highest point since 1998. The catalyst was a fresh escalation in the Middle East. Fresh U.S. military strikes against Iran, combined with a tanker attack in the Strait of Hormuz, sent Brent crude climbing past $92 a barrel, a price roughly 30% above where it stood before the war began. Higher energy costs have heightened expectations of persistent inflation, which in turn has increased the probability that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates. Those expectations were already elevated after Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh, speaking at the Jackson Hole symposium last Friday, signaled that bringing inflation back to target was his undisputed priority, according to Bloomberg. U.S. money markets priced a 65% probability of a rate increase at the Fed's Sept. 16 meeting, up from roughly one-third before Warsh's speech. Economists at Barclays and Societe Generale changed their forecasts after the speech to predict rate hikes they had not previously anticipated, according to Bloomberg. "Global bonds are facing a perfect storm of rising inflation fears, driven by higher energy prices, which are in turn raising rate hike expectations," Leon Ferdinand Bost, analyst at Metzler, said in a note, according to the Journal. "At the same time, fiscal concerns are back at the forefront and together with heavy supply are weighing on the long end." Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi, UBS chief investment officer of the Americas and global head of equities, pointed to a broader set of pressures. "Uncertainty over the Federal Reserve's policy outlook, fiscal concerns, and rising AI-related debt issuance have all kept bonds under pressure," she said in a Tuesday note. "Yield volatility is likely to persist in the near term." Mounting government debt levels have added to investor anxiety. The United States' total public debt surpassed $40 trillion last month, a figure that represents more than 120% of annual economic output, according to the Times. France's sovereign debt has crossed 3.5 trillion euros, equivalent to around 117% of its GDP, and Japan carries an even heavier burden — its government debt stands at more than double the country's entire annual economic output. The current selloff follows a period of acute pressure on long-dated U.S. debt. The 30-year Treasury hit a 19-year high earlier this month, touching 5.323%, a move that has added upward pressure on mortgage rates, auto loan rates, and other consumer borrowing costs. Yields had briefly stabilized in the days that followed before resuming their climb. Join 500,000+ readers who start their day with Quartz. item.title: META's Closed-Loop Cooling Gains Ground: Can it Fuel AI Expansion?
item.description:
Source: Quartz Score: 5.34
Meta $META Platforms META is strengthening its AI infrastructure with more efficient cooling technology as rising compute demand makes data-center efficiency increasingly critical. Building on this momentum, the company recently announced that it is using closed-loop liquid cooling across the majority of its newest AI-optimized data centers to efficiently manage heat generated by increasingly powerful GPUs. The system circulates a water-and-glycol coolant through servers and heat exchangers before reusing it, significantly reducing ongoing water consumption. Meta Platforms expects the coolant to remain usable for up to a decade. Direct-to-chip cooling also enables higher GPU density within server racks, supporting greater computing capacity without substantially expanding data-center space. Meta Platforms is additionally using reinforcement learning to optimize cooling operations across facilities. In a data-center pilot, this approach reduced energy consumed by air-cooling supply fans by an average of 20% and lowered water consumption by 4% across varying weather conditions. These efficiency gains are expected to support Meta Platforms’ broader AI infrastructure expansion as it scales increasingly compute-intensive models and services. The company is deploying AI across recommendations and advertising while developing personal agents, business agents and enterprise offerings, creating multiple avenues to monetize its growing compute capacity. Meta Platforms believes near-term AI capacity remains highly valuable, with numerous ROI-positive opportunities across its core business. In the second quarter of 2026,

item.title: Is Argan's 21% Margin Boost a Sign of Things to Come for Investors?
item.description:
Source: Quartz Score: 5.31
Argan, Inc. AGX delivered a strong start to fiscal 2027, with improving profitability highlighting the benefits of solid project execution and a favorable business mix. The company’s consolidated gross margin expanded to 21% in the first quarter from 19% a year ago, while revenues jumped 50.2% year over year to $291 million. The margin improvement was primarily driven by the Power segment, supported by a shift in project and contract mix, strong execution and the ahead-of-schedule completion of the final Midwest solar and battery project. Power segment gross margin reached 23.6% compared with 11.8% for Industrial and 11% for Teledata. AGX’s profitability metrics also strengthened meaningfully. Net income more than doubled to $46.1 million, or $3.24 per diluted share, from $22.6 million, or $1.60, in the prior-year quarter. Adjusted EBITDA rose 79% to $56.4 million, while the adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 19.4% from 16.3%. However, investors should temper expectations. Management noted that several major projects are still in their early stages, leaving significant risks that could affect ultimate margins. Historically, Argan’s consolidated blended margins tend to range from the high teens to low 20s and can vary based on project timing, mix and execution. The outlook nevertheless remains encouraging. A $2.8-billion backlog, robust demand for complex gas-fired projects and growing data-center infrastructure needs provide a solid foundation. With disciplined project selection and continued execution, Argan appears well-positioned to sustain healthy profitability, although quarterly margins are likely to fluctuate.

item.title: CBRS' Global Expansion Boosts Growth Prospects Against NVDA & MSFT
item.description:
Source: Quartz Score: 5.19
Cerebras Systems CBRS is expanding its international footprint as demand for high-speed Artificial Intelligence (AI) inference rises across enterprises, hyperscalers and sovereign AI initiatives. The company has data centers operational or under contract outside the United States in France, Finland and Norway, as well as Manitoba, Montreal, Saskatchewan and Toronto in Canada. This distributed infrastructure should bring compute closer to customers, broaden Cerebras’ addressable market and strengthen its ability to compete with NVIDIA NVDA and Microsoft $MSFT MSFT in the global AI infrastructure market. Cerebras has secured more than 600 megawatts of data-center capacity that is either live or contracted for delivery by the end of 2027, while its pipeline of additional opportunities is measured in gigawatts. Its inference-focused architecture provides flexibility in selecting sites because it does not require the gigawatt-scale locations typically associated with large training clusters. Cerebras has expanded manufacturing capacity and expects it to increase more than 10-fold in 2026, supporting the infrastructure required for further geographic growth. International markets are already making a meaningful contribution to Cerebras’ business. UAE-based Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence accounted for 34% of revenues in the second quarter of 2026 and 49% in the first half of 2026, while G42 contributed 9% and 10%, respectively. The company’s customer base also includes sovereign AI initiatives, reinforcing the opportunity to serve governments and organizations that require greater control over infrastructure and data. Cerebras supports such customers through on-premises systems, Cerebras Cloud and partner-cloud offerings. CBRS management said the AWS relationship provides global reach, while discussions with other hyperscalers could begin generating revenues in mid-2027 and ramp through 2028. Notably, the roughly $25 billion of remaining performance obligations (RPO) do not include backlog from AWS or other hyperscalers.

item.title: Barclays Gains 34.2% in a Year: Is There Further Upside Potential?
item.description:
Source: Quartz Score: 5.10
Barclays has gained 34.2% over the past year as core growth and stronger earnings support momentum, while elevated costs and regulatory demands pose risks. One-Year Price Performance Image Source: Zacks Investment Research Does BCS stock have more upside left despite recent price strength? Let us find out by looking at its fundamentals and growth prospects. Core Business Expansion: Barclays continues to reshape its portfolio around businesses where it sees higher returns, stronger customer relationships, and scalable growth opportunities. In June 2026, the company announced a deal to acquire GoHenry to strengthen its position in youth banking, while the completed acquisition of Best Egg on May 1, 2026, added digital personal-lending capabilities to the U.S. Consumer Bank. Barclays also announced a new Samsung partnership in the United States, further expanding its consumer-finance ecosystem. These initiatives build on earlier acquisitions, including the General Motors $GM card portfolio in 2025 and Tesco Bank in 2024, as the company continues to exit lower-priority businesses. The strategy is also translating into organic balance sheet growth. Barclays had deployed £25 billion of its approximately £30 billion targeted U.K. business-growth Risk-Weighted Assets (RWAs) by June 2026, including £18 billion from organic growth. U.K. lending increased 5% year over year in the first half of 2026, demonstrating that the company's investments and portfolio repositioning are increasingly supporting underlying loan growth. Barclays remains on track to achieve its 2025-2028 target of more than 5% lending CAGR, providing a stronger foundation for broader customer relationships and future revenue growth. UK Corporate Lending Drives Franchise Growth Image Source: Barclays Broad-Based Revenue Growth: Barclays' operating momentum has extended beyond a single quarter as growth across its core businesses, structural hedge income and Investment Bank activity strengthened revenues. While net interest income and fee-based income experienced volatility over recent quarters amid a challenging operating environment, the company's strategic emphasis on higher-return core businesses is increasingly translating into improved operating performance. The momentum continued in the first half of 2026, with total income reaching £16.5 billion. Management consequently raised its full-year 2026 income target to approximately £31.5 billion from approximately £31 billion and increased its NII guidance, excluding the Investment Bank and Head Office, to more than £13.7 billion from more than £13.5 billion. The structural hedge provides an additional source of visibility, with Barclays expecting it to continue delivering income growth beyond 2028. More than 95% of the relevant hedge contribution was already locked in during the second quarter of 2026, supporting management's target of more than 5% income CAGR between 2025 and 2028. This combination of diversified business growth and structural hedge income should support a more resilient revenue base and longer-term return expansion. Strong Income Growth Drives Momentum Capital Strength Supports Shareholder Returns: Barclays continues to combine improving earnings with substantial shareholder distributions. The company announced £2.3 billion of capital distributions for the first half of 2026, up 61% year over year, comprising approximately £0.8 billion of dividends and £1.5 billion of share buybacks. Since 2024, announced shareholder distributions have reached £9 billion, keeping Barclays on track to achieve its target of at least £10 billion of distributions by the end of 2026. The company is also targeting more than £15 billion of shareholder distributions during 2026-2028 while retaining capacity to invest in growth. Its CET1 ratio was 14.3% as of June 30, 2026, or 14.0% on a pro forma basis for the latest £1 billion buyback, placing capital at the top end of management's 13-14% target range. This suggests that Barclays' improving earnings and capital generation can continue supporting both business investment and shareholder returns. Strong Shareholders Returns Elevated Costs and Credit Expenses: Barclays continues to face pressure from rising operating expenses and elevated credit impairment charges. Despite achieving £1.7 billion in gross structural savings in 2024 and 2025, the company continues to invest in growth, technology and operating changes, keeping near-term expenses elevated. Management targets more than £2 billion in total gross efficiency savings and a cost-to-income ratio in the low 50s by 2028, but expects up to £500 million of additional structural cost actions in the second half of 2026. Credit impairment charges also remain elevated, having recorded a 23.2% CAGR from 2022 to 2025, with the upward trend continuing in the first half of 2026. Management expects the 2026 loan loss rate to remain around the top end of its 50-60 basis-point through-the-cycle range. Together, elevated operating and credit costs could weigh on Barclays' near-term profitability. Regulatory Capital Demands: Barclays expects £19-£26 billion of regulatory RWA inflation in 2027, including the impact of Basel 3.1 changes and the U.S. Consumer Bank's move to an internal ratings-based model. While the CET1 ratio was 14.3% as of June 30, 2026, additional regulatory RWAs could compete with business growth and shareholder distributions for capital. Although lower Pillar 2A requirements may provide some offset, execution of Barclays' more than £15 billion shareholder distribution plan for 2026-2028 will depend on continued capital generation and regulatory clarity. The Zacks Consensus Estimate points to sustained earnings growth over the next two years. The consensus estimates for 2026 earnings of $2.83 per share and 2027 earnings of $3.41 indicate continued earnings momentum. This growth, combined with recent share-price strength, supports Barclays’ near-term outlook. Earnings Estimate In terms of its valuation, Barclays stock is currently trading at a trailing 12-month price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 10.03, compared with the industry average of 13.66. This indicates that BCS is currently trading at a discount to its industry. P/E TTM Barclays also trades at a discount compared with Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs. At present, Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs trade at a trailing 12-month P/E of 17.37X and 16.07X, respectively. Is There Room for Further Upside for Barclays? Despite Barclays’ improving revenue momentum, stronger capital position and progress in its core franchises, the stock does not appear to offer a compelling risk-reward profile at present. The bank remains exposed to elevated operating and credit costs, while substantial regulatory RWA inflation expected in 2027 could constrain capital available for growth and shareholder distributions. These headwinds could limit near-term upside if revenue growth moderates or credit costs remain elevated. Nonetheless, Barclays’ earnings trajectory and capital generation offer support.
