The four-day Tree to Waterfall hike covers 29 miles and costs 6,100,000 rupiah (around £276) all inclusive, astungkaraway.com Dinner in a South African township Township and Village (a finalist in the 2025 ICRT Global responsible tourism awards) welcomes visitors into communities in the town of Stellenbosch and its surrounding vineyards to experience day-to-day life in the Western Cape province. Launched in 2023, the social enterprise offers a host of activities, from dining on traditional Xhosa cuisine at a family home in the Kayamandi township, to djembe drumming sessions and guided walks to learn more about the area’s cultures and turbulent history. Community-based guides ensure authentic encounters, and visitors contribute directly to the local economy. A three-course home dining experience is 550 rand (around £23), townshipandvillage.co.za

item.title: A slow travel success story in Slovenia’s secret valley
item.description:
Source: The Guardian Travel Score: 2.44
The drive to Pedrovo is vertiginous, and each hairpin bend has me sending a silent prayer that we won’t meet a tractor coming the other way. When we near it, we abandon the car and continue on foot to the hamlet, a scattering of red-roofed, whitewashed houses high on the steep karst hillside. The air is warm and dry, scented with wild sage. We follow a hand-painted sign to Čilčevi Farmstead. Descending stone steps to a lush garden, we find a shaded table set with fresh cheeses produced at the farm’s own dairy. Below, the valley stretches in both directions, a wide flat plain hemmed in by steep mountain slopes, with the Vipava River winding lazily through fields and vineyards. If the Vipava valley gets a mention in a Slovenian guidebook, it’s usually as a wine region footnote. The area is an hour’s drive south-west of Ljubljana, meeting Italy at the cross-border city of Nova Gorica (called Gorizia on the Italian side). Most visitors skip it in favour of the Soča valley to the north, drawn to the turquoise river and opportunities for rafting on the rapids. Vipava is a landscape shaped by a strong wind, the burja, which barrels down from the Alps, keeping the red earth arid, the trees bent low, and creating the perfect terrain for dry wines and dried meats. Tourism has traditionally been less of a focus, but I’m here with my family to meet local entrepreneurs and producers, to learn how this valley is building a genuine visitor experience that works for the community. Part of the reason for the slow development of tourism has been the scarcity of accommodation, save a few nondescript business hotels and a handful of holiday cottages. One place that’s helping change that narrative is Wellba, a boutique guesthouse in the village of Planina, where an old abandoned farmstead has been converted into self-catering apartments and guest rooms by a local couple, working with traditional craftspeople and salvaged materials. Marko and Tereza Kobal grew up on this hillside and then worked in Ljubljana before deciding to return to build a family business, striving to create the kind of place they seek out when travelling. “People who travel want to experience something that is just the way it is, without embellishment, pretence, exaggeration – somewhere authentic,” says Marko. We enter Wellba through a traditional “black kitchen”, its walls darkened by generations of wood smoke. “When we came here the building needed work but it had a real soul. We want the building to stand for another 300 years, so we took the renovation slowly and carefully.” Our light, spacious accommodation wears its history lightly, with plenty of space for playing card games and reading books on the balcony, with views of the neighbouring farmyard and the valley beyond. Next door, another tumble-down farm building will be converted and opened in 2027. The couple are also working on a boutique hotel in Vipava town in the valley below. The dream is for their children to run Wellba one day, forging their futures in this valley. Across Vipava, similar small projects are emerging: small, family-run and developing slowly and thoughtfully. Tom Ločniškar and Borut Kokalj began Čilčevi Farmstead during the pandemic, having moved to Pedrovo and become interested in farming. “We started to keep animals. Now we have 150, which is too many animals for just a hobby,” laughs Tom. He recalls the mad panic to source equipment before the lockdowns began. The pandemic also brought him his first customers, people who were out walking and keen to support local businesses. Tom and Borut keep local Istrska sheep and Drežnica goats, which graze on dry karst grasslands, changing pastures across this hillside every four days. Having tasted fresh cheese straight from the chill of the dairy, including creamy goat’s cheese with fenugreek and buttery mature sheep’s cheese, we walk uphill to meet the goats. Tom says that in the early 1900s around 1,000 people lived in Pedrovo, but by the 1970s the permanent population had fallen to just two, and remained that low until the 1990s. “The village was almost abandoned because people moved to the cities,” he says. “It was the same in a lot of hill villages: life was hard and tractors didn’t work on steep slopes.” Today the population has risen to 20, with second homeowners roughly doubling that number in the holidays. Elsewhere in the village, I meet Alenka and Mark Smerajc, who were one of the first families to return, raising three children and running a business here. Today they have two small holiday cottages in what were farm outbuildings and run a relaxed courtyard restaurant for guests, opening to the public at weekends and for holidays. “People wanted food,” shrugs Alenka, as her teenage children help bring out beautiful plates of handmade pasta with local cheese and wild herbs from the kitchen. “In Vipava valley there was no tourism, so we got to decide how to build it,” says Jani Peljhan. That means GPS-guided cycling tours along roads too small to merit signposts, and experimenting with “wine trains”, carrying visitors from Nova Gorica to the vineyards with local winemakers on board to lead tasting sessions. Jani’s company, Wajdušna, also offers hiking and paragliding, both gaining in popularity here. He meets us at Wellba with some e-bikes and we pedal through Ajdovščina to spot Roman ruins, and up to Vipavski Križ, famed for being one of the smallest towns in Slovenia, before zigzagging back up the other side of the valley through vineyards. The warmth of the afternoon and the steep hillsides makes me appreciate the “sport” mode on the bikes. In other regions, wine tourism often means visitor centres and branded experiences. In Vipava it still means sitting in someone’s kitchen. At Vina Lisjak in Zalošče, I eat at a little restaurant run by two brothers. “We opened the restaurant to show the wine,” says Peter Lisjak. “It’s all from our farm.” We eat generous platters of house dried meat, aged mountain cheeses, a fennel frittata and slow-cooked celeriac steaks with celery pesto and spinach. Dishes are served family style and there’s plenty of time for stories, with samples of delicious wine straight from the barrels in the cellar. From Wellba, we walk across the village to Ferjančič vineyard, where seventh generation winemaker Matic Ferjančič talks us through his wines. His father developed the vineyard, going from five to 50,000 plants. “We work hard in the vineyard to make it easy in the cellar,” he says. As we chat, Matic keeps an ear to the baby monitor for the eighth generation sleeping upstairs. Although many of my favourite restaurant experiences are the simple ones, Vipava valley cuisine can reach loftier heights. One night we smarten up the best we can and follow a winding road uphill to Zemono Manor, to eat at Gostilna Pri Lojzetu. Chef Tomaž Kavčič is known as a Slovenian slow food pioneer, and has earned a Michelin star for his playful dishes and proud use of local ingredients. We eat delicate Vipava river trout with fermented apricots from the previous summer, and langoustine bisque from the coast. Traditional dishes such as jota, a sauerkraut and potato stew, are honoured on the menu, their humble roots celebrated not hidden. There are some theatrics, like a juniper plant producing flavoured vapour to complement a sorbet, but the restaurant atmosphere is friendly and relaxed. The server chats with my young stepson about his preferences, and brings him a generous bowl of gnocchi. It’s Kavčič’s night off so he sits with friends and a bottle of wine at the back of the restaurant, coming round all the tables frequently to chat. Vipava may not remain overlooked for ever. But talking to the people building businesses here, there is little appetite for becoming the next famous wine destination. What they seem to want instead is something rarer and more interesting: tourism that helps a place thrive without changing what made it worth visiting in the first place. The trip was provided by Vipava Valley Tourism and the Slovenian Tourist Board. Wellba Planina has doubles from £97

item.title: Rove adds Copa ConnectMiles as a transfer partner, offering a limited-time 40% bonus
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 5.79
Rove adds Copa ConnectMiles as a transfer partner, offering a limited-time 40% bonus Rove just announced its newest transfer partner: Copa Airlines ConnectMiles. To celebrate the new partnership, Rove is offering a 40% transfer bonus to Copa ConnectMiles through Sept. 30. This transfer bonus means that you'll get 1,400 ConnectMiles for every 1,000 Rove miles that you transfer to Copa through Sept. 30. Copa ConnectMiles is a lesser-known Star Alliance program. But while the program isn't as well known, its region-based award charts offer some potentially useful sweet spots. Here's everything to know about this new partnership and why it may make sense to take advantage of this transfer bonus. Not a Rove member yet? Sign up through this link and earn a referral bonus of 1,500 miles, with the opportunity to earn an additional 5,000 miles when making your first hotel booking over $500 as a new user with the code "BRIANKELLY500." Rove adds Copa ConnectMiles as a transfer partner Rove miles will typically transfer to Copa ConnectMiles at a 1:1 ratio. But through Sept. 30, Rove members can transfer miles to Copa at a 1:1.4 ratio. Copa ConnectMiles is Rove's 21st transfer partner, and it's a particularly noteworthy addition because it isn't a transfer partner of any of the major credit card rewards currencies. You can transfer Marriott Bonvoy points to Copa at a 3:1 ratio, but Rove is the first major transferable currency available to U.S. residents that lets its members transfer rewards to Copa at a 1:1 ratio. Related: Rove adds dining and in-store rewards in major platform expansion Why the 40% Copa transfer bonus could be valuable Copa ConnectMiles uses region-based award charts. It publishes an award chart for its own flights with saver and standard award pricing, and it also prices partner awards by region. However, the partner award chart currently available on Copa's website appears outdated, so you'll want to check the current pricing for partner awards by searching directly with ConnectMiles. Note that you may see two rates for United Airlines-operated flights when searching for awards on Copa's website, as Copa offers both saver and standard awards for United flights. All this being said, here are some one-way award sweet spots to consider when redeeming Copa miles: - Flights from U.S. or Canadian destinations to Dubai in Emirates business class for 80,000 Copa miles - Transcontinental flights in United business class for 25,000 Copa miles (if you find saver award space) - Flights from Panama to southern South American destinations in Copa economy for 20,000 Copa miles or Copa business class for 40,000 Copa miles (if you find saver award space) You can usually transfer Rove miles in increments of 100 as long as you transfer at least 2,000 miles. Keep in mind, though, that you must check award availability with Copa ConnectMiles — don't rely on seeing award space on another airline's website. And while you can book many partner-operated awards — such as those operated by United, Turkish Airlines, Avianca and Lufthansa — on the ConnectMiles website, you'll need to call to book awards operated by some partners. ConnectMiles also generally doesn't pass along carrier-imposed surcharges on partner awards. That alone can make it worth checking ConnectMiles pricing before booking the same award through another loyalty program. Bottom line Rove has added Copa ConnectMiles to an already impressive roster of transfer partners, including other popular Star Alliance loyalty programs like Air Canada Aeroplan, Lufthansa Miles & More and Turkish Miles&Smiles. As such, ConnectMiles likely won't be the program you use to book most Star Alliance awards. However, since Marriott Bonvoy is the only major transferable program available to U.S. residents that partners with Copa ConnectMiles, and because ConnectMiles typically doesn't pass on carrier-imposed surcharges, this is still a valuable addition. And with the 40% transfer bonus through Sept. 30, now is a great time for Rove members to see whether ConnectMiles' award charts can provide compelling value on select awards.

item.title: United's Airbus A321XLR is about to make its (domestic) debut: Here are the routes
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 5.43
United's Airbus A321XLR is about to make its (domestic) debut: Here are the routes Who doesn't like that new-plane smell? United Airlines travelers can look forward to the scent onboard its brand-new Airbus A321XLRs when they begin flying in September. Ahead of the new aircraft's global debut in December, you can experience the new long-range narrow-body aircraft on some domestic services. United will christen the XLR on flights from its Dulles International Airport (IAD) hub to San Diego International Airport (SAN) on Sept. 9 and to Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) on Oct. 1, a spokesperson confirmed Friday. Long-range aircraft goes domestic (for now) The XLRs are United's newest plane. They're designed especially for longer flights, with 20 lie-flat Polaris business-class suites up front in a 1-1 layout. There are also 12 Premium Plus (premium economy) recliners arranged in a 2-2 layout. In the back are 34 extra-legroom Economy Plus seats in a 3-3 layout — except for four seats where the middle seat is blocked — along with 84 standard economy seats. There's even a snack bar for all passengers at the back of the cabin. United has orders for 50 XLRs that will primarily fly transatlantic flights from its IAD and Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) hubs. The airline will shift the XLR to long-haul flights Dec. 1 when it begins flying daily between IAD and both Amsterdam Airport Schiphol (AMS) and Dublin Airport (DUB). And, next summer, the XLR is headlining United's blockbuster 2027 transatlantic expansion, flying five of nine new routes, including to Ibiza, Spain; Luxembourg; and Toulouse, France. But for the next few months, the plane will operate some transcontinental service domestically — something executives had suggested this week could happen, albeit on a temporary basis. Booking United's new Airbus A321XLR For anyone looking to fly on the XLR before its international debut, MileagePlus award tickets are available on IAD-SAN for as few as 12,700 miles in economy for Sept. 9. And, if they are lucky, travelers can snag one of the new premium economy seats sold as just an extra-legroom economy option. First-class seats are available later in September, starting at 85,000 miles. Bottom line United ultimately plans to focus its new XLR on long-haul international service. But with its luxe new domestic airplane delayed and crews still adapting to this new aircraft, it's not surprising to see the new aircraft make its debut on the domestic front — at least for a few months. item.title: What are points and miles worth? TPG's September 2026 monthly valuations
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 5.23
What are points and miles worth? TPG's September 2026 monthly valuations Editor's Note One of the questions people often ask us is, "How much is a point or mile worth?" The true answer varies from point to point and person to person. It also depends on your travel goals and how much you maximize a particular loyalty currency. Still, some rewards are worth more than others, and our goal is to give you a sense of how they stack up. Related: How TPG determines its points and miles valuations View this post on Instagram What are credit card points and miles worth? | Program | September 2026 valuation (cents) | Latest news | |---|---|---| | American Express Membership Rewards | 2.0 | Amex added more than 350 hotels to its Fine Hotels + Resorts and The Hotel Collection collections. Amex also extended the Resy credit to Tock restaurants and brought back a long-awaited transfer bonus to Avios. | | Capital One | 1.85 | | | Chase Ultimate Rewards | 2.05 | | | Citi ThankYou Rewards | 1.9 | | | Wells Fargo Rewards | 1.75 | | What are Bilt Points worth? | Program | September 2026 valuation (cents) | Latest news | |---|---|---| | Bilt | 2.2 | | What are airline points and miles worth? | Program | September 2026 valuation (cents) | Latest news | |---|---|---| | Aeromexico Rewards | 0.8 | | | Air Canada Aeroplan | 1.5 (up from 1.45)* | | | Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards | 1.55* | | | American Airlines AAdvantage | 1.45 (up from 1.4)* | American added Vienna, Reykjavik and Porto as part of a seven-route international expansion and confirmed that seatback screens would return across all cabins in 2028. American raised Admirals Club membership prices and introduced a cheaper solo option. The Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® also received a major refresh. American Airlines Vacations also launched a promotion offering up to 11 miles and Loyalty Points per dollar. | | ANA Mileage Club | 1.4 | | | Avianca Lifemiles | 1.55 (up from 1.45)* | | | Avios | 1.4 | | | Cathay Asia Miles | 1.3 | | | Delta SkyMiles | 1.2* | Delta cut America's longest domestic flight for a second time. The airline made clear it was no fan of single-aisle long-haul flying. The Delta-Aeromexico joint venture won a reprieve after a termination order was dismissed. | | Emirates Skywards | 1.2 | | | Etihad Guest | 1.2 | | | Flying Blue | 1.4 (down from 1.45)* | | | Frontier Miles | 1.3 | | | JetBlue TrueBlue | 1.35 | | | Qantas Frequent Flyer | 1.2 (down from 1.25)* | | | Singapore KrisFlyer | 1.3 | | | Southwest Rapid Rewards | 1.25 | | | Turkish Airlines Miles&Smiles | 1.1 | | | United MileagePlus | 1.2 (down from 1.25)* | United added 10 new international destinations in the largest route announcement in its history, and confirmed its off-the-beaten-path international routes would return in 2027. The airline revealed the domestic debut routes for its Airbus A321XLR but ended its Newark-Lima service. United's targeted Mile Play promotion returned. | | Virgin Atlantic Flying Club | 1.45* | | *Calculated using data provided by Points Path. What are hotel points worth? | Program | September 2026 valuation (cents) | Latest news | |---|---|---| | Accor Live Limitless | 2.3 | | | Best Western Rewards | 0.6 | | | Choice Privileges | 0.85 (up from 0.7)** | | | Hilton Honors | 0.4 ** | | | IHG One Rewards | 0.6 (up from 0.55)** | | | Marriott Bonvoy | 0.75** | | | World of Hyatt | 1.65 (up from 1.6)** | | | Wyndham Rewards | 0.7** | | **Calculated using data from Gondola (a free hotel search and direct booking platform for frequent travelers). Top points and miles news for September August was a huge month for new long-haul route announcements, especially to Europe, opening up more destinations to redeem your points and miles. United unveiled 10 new international destinations across 13 routes for summer 2027, the largest announcement of its kind in the airline's history, including the first U.S. nonstop flights to Slovenia and Luxembourg. American answered two days later, adding Vienna, Reykjavik and Porto among seven new international routes and will become the only U.S. carrier flying to Vienna when service begins in May. Many of these new routes are possible thanks to both airlines' new Airbus A321XLRs, single-aisle aircraft capable of flying deep into Europe. With fewer seats to fill than a wide-body aircraft, American and United can launch flights to lesser-known destinations. For passengers, the convenience is nonstop service from major U.S. airports to destinations that previously required a connection. The trade-off is the onboard experience, which may not be as comfortable as flying on larger planes, with business-class seats facing the aisle rather than the window and potentially longer waits for fewer bathrooms. You can expect the most plentiful award availability for these new flights to be offered through the American Airlines AAdvantage program (for American Airlines flights) and United's MileagePlus program (for United flights). As both programs use dynamic pricing for their flights, redemption rates may be high during peak travel periods, such as summer school holidays. As such, it's also worth searching partner programs (try British Airways Club for American Airlines flights and Air Canada Aeroplan for United flights) that don't dynamically price these flights. Availability will be worse than booking through American AAdvantage or United MileagePlus, but the rates may be lower. Most of the new flights launch between March and June 2027 and run seasonally, which is worth keeping in mind when searching for award space. A handy tip is to search the first and last few weeks of the schedule, where you may find award availability more readily available and lower-priced. Related: 9 European summer destinations to beat the heat Top offers for earning points and miles in September September's cobranded credit card offer of the month is the suite of Atmos Rewards credit cards, where you can earn up to 80,000 bonus Atmos Rewards points, companion awards and more. Here are some of the best welcome offers this month for those seeking a new travel rewards card that earns transferable points or miles. - American Express Platinum Card®: Find out your offer and see if you are eligible for as high as 175,000 Membership Rewards points after spending $12,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. Welcome offers vary, and you may not be eligible for an offer. - Capital One Venture X Rewards Credit Card: Earn 75,000 bonus miles when you spend $4,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. - Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card: Earn 75,000 miles once you spend $4,000 on purchases within three months from account opening. - Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card (see rates and fees): Earn 75,000 bonus points after you spend $5,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. - American Express® Gold Card: Find out your offer and see if you are eligible for as high as 100,000 Membership Rewards points after spending $8,000 on purchases within the first six months of card membership. Welcome offers vary, and you may not be eligible for an offer. - Chase Sapphire Reserve® (see rates and fees): Earn 100,000 bonus points after you spend $6,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. - Capital One Venture X Business: Earn 150,000 bonus miles once you spend $30,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. Frequently asked questions A points and miles valuation estimates how much a loyalty currency is worth, typically expressed in cents per point or mile. TPG uses these valuations to compare rewards programs and help travelers decide when to earn, redeem or transfer rewards. TPG valuations are estimates based on factors such as award pricing, redemption opportunities, fees, program rules and extensive redemption data. However, the value you get when redeeming your rewards may be higher or lower depending on your goals, flexibility and how effectively you maximize a particular rewards currency. A good redemption value is one that meets or exceeds TPG's published valuation for a particular points or miles currency. While exceptional redemptions can deliver even greater value, our valuations provide a practical benchmark to help travelers determine whether they're getting a strong return from their rewards. Based on TPG's September 2026 valuations, Bilt points are the most valuable transferable rewards currency at 2.2 cents per point. Chase Ultimate Rewards points rank second at 2.05 cents per point, followed by American Express Membership Rewards at 2.0 cents, Citi ThankYou Rewards at 1.9 cents and Capital One miles at 1.85 cents. Based on TPG's September 2026 valuations, Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards is the most valuable airline currency at 1.55 cents per point. Atmos Rewards earns this distinction because it continues to offer strong redemption opportunities on flights with Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines, as well as on flights with its partners. Based on TPG's September 2026 valuations, Accor Live Limitless points are the most valuable hotel currency at 2.3 cents per point, followed by World of Hyatt points at 1.65 cents per point. Accor points have a fixed redemption value, while Hyatt's award charts can help members secure outsize value on some hotel stays. item.title: 32 new Hyatt hotels where you can get 500 extra points per night
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.69
32 new Hyatt hotels where you can get 500 extra points per night Editor's Note World of Hyatt offers 500 bonus points per night on qualifying stays at new hotels. Although 500 bonus points might not sound like a lot, they are worth $8 based on TPG's September 2026 valuations. Hyatt doesn't require members to register for this promotion, so you may have forgotten (or never known) about it. Here's a quick look at the World of Hyatt promotion that allows you to earn 500 bonus points per night at new hotels. Earn 500 points per night at new Hyatt hotels The promotion is simple: World of Hyatt members receive 500 bonus points per night for qualifying stays at select hotels new to the Hyatt portfolio. You must stay within a set time frame to earn the bonus points, typically in the first few months after the property opens. Specifically, you'll earn bonus points only if your checkout date falls within your hotel's offer period. To earn bonus points, you must provide your World of Hyatt number when checking in. You must also pay an eligible rate or redeem a Hyatt free night certificate (including Hyatt points), but groups, conventions, other promotional offers, tour packages and special rate programs aren't eligible. You'll only earn bonus points for one room per night. The terms of this promotion state that it may take three to four weeks for the bonus points to appear in your account. In practice, though, Hyatt typically posts the new-hotel bonus with the other points you earned during your stay. Related: Best Hyatt hotels in the world to book with points Eligible new Hyatt hotels Hyatt regularly updates a list of participating properties. Here's an overview of where you can currently earn 500 extra points per night. 13 new Hyatt hotels in the US - Arden, North Carolina: Hyatt Place Asheville Airport from Sept. 24 to Dec. 31 - Chesapeake, Virginia: Hyatt Studios Chesapeake until Sept. 30 - Essington, Pennsylvania: Hyatt Select Philadelphia Airport until Oct. 31 - Jeffersonville, Indiana: Hyatt Select Louisville North until Nov. 30 - Mechanicsburg, Pennsylvania: Hyatt Studios Mechanicsburg from Sept. 23 to Dec. 31 - Reviews Delta SkyMiles Reserve Business card review: Premium perks for Delta loyalists Stephanie Stevens is an associate writer with TPG's credit cards team. She focuses on creating timely credit cards content for TPG readers. August 29, 2026 • 16 min read The cards we feature here are from partners who compensate us when you are approved through our site, and this may impact how or where these products appear. We don't cover all available credit cards, but our analysis, reviews, and opinions are entirely from our editorial team. Terms apply to the offers listed on this page. Please view our advertising policy and product review methodology for more information. Editorial note: This is a recurring post, regularly updated with new information and offers. Editorial disclaimer: Opinions expressed here are the author's alone, not those of any bank, credit card issuer, airline or hotel chain, and have not been reviewed, approved or otherwise endorsed by any of these entities. Related stories Quick summary A premium business travel card offers significant benefits for frequent flyers with one major airline, including airport lounge access, annual companion certificates and elite-status advantages. The card is best suited for business owners who regularly travel with this airline and can maximize perks like lounge visits and statement credits for travel, dining and ride-hailing. Key benefits include 15 annual lounge visits (with unlimited access possible after high annual spending), complimentary checked bags, priority boarding and discounts on award flights. Drawbacks include a high annual fee, limited earning rates outside select categories and a substantial spending requirement for unlimited lounge access. What to consider Enrollment is required for select statement credits and benefits. Companion certificate availability may be limited on certain routes and dates, requiring advance planning. Unlimited lounge access requires substantial annual spending, and the card's value is best realized by those loyal to the airline. What you'll miss from the article A detailed comparison of premium business travel cards, including trade-offs between lounge access, elite-status perks and overall value for different types of travelers. Generated by AI with support from our editorial team. Earn 3 miles per dollar on eligible Delta purchases. Intro offer Earn 200,000 Bonus Miles Annual fee $650 Regular APR 19.49% - 28.49% Variable Recommended credit Excellent to Good The is Delta Air Lines' most premium business credit card, and is best suited for business owners who fly Delta frequently and want airport lounge access, elite-status benefits and premium travel perks. The card's $650 annual fee (see rates and fees) is undeniably expensive. However, for frequent Delta flyers, benefits like Delta Sky Club access, an annual companion certificate, statement credits and Medallion Qualification Dollar (MQD) earning opportunities can help justify the cost. Enrollment is required for select benefits. Card rating*: ⭐⭐⭐½ *Card rating is based on the opinion of TPG’s editors and is not influenced by the card issuer. Delta Reserve Business Amex: The basics The is designed for frequent Delta travelers who want premium travel benefits and a faster path toward Delta Medallion status. Here's what you need to know: Annual fee: $650 Best for: Business owners and frequent Delta flyers seeking lounge access, elite-status benefits and premium travel perks Rewards structure: Elevated earnings on Delta purchases and bonus miles on select business spending categories Key benefits: Delta Sky Club access (subject to limitations) , annual companion certificate, MQD earning through spending, statement credits and travel perks when flying Delta Rewards currency: Delta SkyMiles, best redeemed for Delta flights and partner award travel In my opinion, the biggest reason to carry this card is its collection of premium travel benefits that can make frequent Delta travel significantly more comfortable. Delta Reserve Business Amex pros and cons Pros Cons Access to Delta Sky Clubs when flying Delta An annual companion certificate Elite status boost Steep annual fee Limited earning rates apart from Delta purchases High spending requirement for unlimited Sky Club access Delta Reserve Business Amex benefits The Delta Reserve Business Amex offers a collection of impressive benefits. Delta Sky Club access Airport lounge access is the primary reason many travelers choose the . Cardmembers receive 15 annual visits to Delta Sky Clubs when flying Delta. Those who spend $75,000 or more on the card during a calendar year unlock unlimited Sky Club visits for the remainder of that year and the following Medallion year. Cardmembers also receive four one-time guest passes each year. TPG editor-in-chief Nick Ewen says lounge access is one of the main reasons he continues to carry the Delta Reserve family of cards. "I love how this card helps elevate my travel — including a headstart toward Medallion qualification each year as well as 15 Sky Club visits each year," he said. "Plus, with the four annual guest passes, I can bring my daughter in and avoid the extra fee." If you regularly travel through Delta hubs, such as Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL) and Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), lounge access can significantly improve your airport experience. I believe this benefit is where many cardholders will derive the majority of the card's value. Annual companion certificate Each year after account renewal, cardmembers receive a companion certificate valid for a round-trip flight in first class, Delta Comfort+ or the Main Cabin. The certificate can be used on eligible flights within the U.S. and to select destinations in Mexico, the Caribbean and Central America. For travelers who would otherwise pay for these tickets in cash, this benefit can easily offset a substantial portion of the card's annual fee. For example, Nick recently used a Delta companion certificate to book first-class flights for himself and his daughter from Orlando to Salt Lake City, saving more than $1,200 compared to purchasing both tickets outright. Like most companion certificates, flexibility is important, as availability can be limited on some routes and dates. In Nick's experience, planning well in advance helped him find eligible first-class availability and maximize the certificate's value. A faster path to Delta Medallion status For business owners pursuing Delta Medallion status, the Delta Reserve Business Amex offers some of the strongest status-earning benefits among Delta's cobranded cards. Cardmembers receive 2,500 MQDs automatically each Medallion qualification year through MQD Headstart. In addition, cardmembers earn 1 MQD for every $10 spent on eligible purchases. Ewen upgraded to the card specifically because of its status-earning potential, saying, "The additional MQD boost plus more Sky Club visits ensure I have plenty of room to enjoy my regular flights with Delta." For businesses with significant annual expenses, these MQD benefits can make it substantially easier to qualify for Medallion status. Valuable perks when flying Delta In addition to status-earning benefits and lounge access, the includes several travel perks that can make every Delta trip smoother and more affordable. Zone 5 priority boarding, out of eight boarding zones A 15% discount on Delta-operated award flights through TakeOff 15, which provides a 15% discount when booking through delta.com or the Fly Delta app Complimentary upgrade eligibility for cardmembers without Medallion status (when available) Savings on eligible Delta inflight purchases I particularly like the TakeOff 15 benefit because it creates ongoing value every time you redeem SkyMiles. If you're regularly booking award flights, those discounts can add up quickly over the course of a year. The complimentary upgrade benefit is worth noting as well. While upgrades are never guaranteed, it's rare for non-elite cardmembers to receive access to an airline's upgrade list simply by holding a credit card. Delta Stays, dining and ride-hailing statement credits The card also offers several statement credits that can help offset its annual fee. Cardmembers can receive: Up to $250 per calendar year in statement credits on eligible Delta Stays bookings Up to $240 per calendar year in statement credits for eligible U.S. Resy purchases (up to $20 monthly) Up to $120 per calendar year in statement credits on eligible U.S. ride-hailing purchases (up to $10 monthly) Enrollment is required for select benefits. As with most credits, I wouldn't automatically value them at face value. However, if you're already using Delta Stays, dining at U.S. Resy restaurants or taking ride-hailing trips throughout the year, these statement credits can help meaningfully reduce the card's effective cost. Additional travel benefits The Delta Reserve Business Amex rounds out its premium benefits package with several additional travel perks. I wouldn't apply for the card solely because of these benefits, but they help reinforce the card's premium positioning. Travel protections can be especially useful when plans don't go as expected, while Hertz President's Circle status can provide a better rental experience for frequent travelers. How to earn and use your rewards Earning Delta SkyMiles With the , you'll earn: 3 miles per dollar spent on eligible Delta purchases 1.5 miles per dollar spent on eligible transit, U.S. shipping and U.S. office supply store purchases 1 mile per dollar spent on all other eligible purchases While the card offers bonus earnings in a handful of categories, I don't think the Delta Reserve Business Amex is particularly compelling for everyday spending unless you're primarily focused on earning MQDs toward Medallion status. Many business rewards cards offer stronger earning rates and more flexible rewards. For me, the value proposition with the Delta Reserve Business centers on the travel perks rather than maximizing mileage earnings. Redeeming Delta SkyMiles The best way to use Delta SkyMiles is generally for flights on Delta and its airline partners. Because Delta uses dynamic award pricing, redemption rates can vary significantly depending on demand, route and travel dates. That means you won't always find predictable award pricing, but there are still plenty of opportunities to get strong value from your miles. I particularly like Delta's SkyMiles Deals, which frequently feature discounted award flights both within the U.S. and internationally. We've seen award sales offering domestic round-trip flights for as few as 13,000 to 20,000 miles and international deals that can save travelers tens of thousands of miles compared to standard pricing. We've also seen excellent value on international awards. For example, TPG's managing editor for points and loyalty programs, Lyndsey Matthews, booked Delta's nonstop flight from John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) to Malta International Airport (MLA) for 47,800 SkyMiles plus $46 in taxes and fees, a ticket that was selling for roughly $969 in cash. Closer to home, TPG managing editor Madison Blancaflor redeemed 40,500 SkyMiles (plus $12 in taxes and fees) for a round-trip ticket from Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) to Bill and Hillary Clinton National Airport (LIT) in Little Rock that would have cost about $700. Remember, one of the biggest advantages of carrying a Delta cobranded card is the TakeOff 15 benefit, which provides a 15% discount on eligible Delta-operated award flights booked through delta.com or the Fly Delta app. That discount effectively stretches your SkyMiles balance further with every redemption. While Delta-operated flights are often the easiest redemption option, I find that partner awards can sometimes provide better value, especially for international premium-cabin travel. Potential drawbacks of the Delta Reserve Business Amex The biggest drawback is the card's $650 annual fee. Even with lounge access, statement credits and an annual companion certificate, that's a significant amount to pay each year. If you're not flying Delta regularly, it can be difficult to justify the cost. The card's earning structure is another weakness. Outside of Delta purchases and a few business-related spending categories, you'll only earn 1 mile per dollar spent on purchases. Many business cards offer higher earning rates and more flexible point currencies. Finally, unlimited Sky Club access requires $75,000 in annual spending. While 15 visits will be sufficient for many, frequent travelers may find that the cap is restrictive. That said, I believe the card makes the most sense for travelers who are committed to Delta. If you're splitting your flights among multiple airlines, many of the card's best benefits become less valuable. Delta Reserve Business Amex vs. Delta Platinum Business Amex Business owners considering the should also take a look at the . The Platinum Business version offers a lower annual fee of $350 (see rates and fees) while still providing an annual companion certificate, a 2,500 MQD Headstart each Medallion qualification year and the ability to earn additional MQDs through card spending. It also includes valuable Delta travel perks, such as a free first checked bag, a free second checked bag on U.S. domestic Delta-operated flights, priority boarding and a 15% discount on eligible Delta-operated award flights through TakeOff 15. However, the Reserve Business Amex is the better choice for travelers who value lounge access. The Platinum Business card does not include Delta Sky Club access, which is arguably the Reserve Business card's most valuable benefit. For frequent Delta travelers who regularly visit lounges and prioritize premium travel perks, I think the additional annual fee can be worthwhile. For everyone else, the Platinum Business version may offer a better balance of cost and benefits. Is the Delta Reserve Business Amex worth it? For the right traveler, absolutely. I think the is easiest to justify for business owners who fly Delta frequently, use airport lounges regularly and are working toward Medallion status. If you won't take advantage of its benefits, however, it becomes much harder to offset the card's substantial annual fee. New cardmembers can earn 200,000 bonus miles after spending $20,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. Offer ends Nov. 4. Based on TPG's September 2026 valuation of Delta SkyMiles at 1.2 cents each, this welcome offer is worth a whopping $2,400. This is by far the highest welcome bonus we've ever seen on this card — but it also requires spending $20,000 on purchases in the first six months. (The previous highest was 125,000 bonus miles after spending $15,000 on purchases in the first six months; offer no longer available). Other cards to consider if you don't want the Delta Reserve Business Amex If Delta Sky Club access and Medallion-status benefits are your primary goals, the is likely your best option. However, another card may be a better fit depending on your priorities. If you want a Delta card with a lower annual fee: The is a solid option for occasional Delta flyers who want valuable airline perks without paying for premium benefits they may not use. For a reasonable annual fee ($0 introductory annual fee for the first year, then $150; see rates and fees), cardmembers receive perks like a free first checked bag on Delta-operated flights and a free second checked bag on U.S. domestic Delta-operated flights. To learn more, check out our full review of the Delta Gold Business Amex. If you want more flexible rewards: earns Membership Rewards points that can be transferred to Delta and numerous other airline and hotel partners. It also provides extensive lounge access and premium travel benefits. To learn more, check out our full review of the Amex Business Platinum. If you want to maximize business spending: The offers strong earning rates across popular business spending categories and earns flexible, transferable Membership Rewards points. To learn more, check out our full review of the Amex Business Gold. I wouldn't recommend it to every business owner. However, for travelers who frequently fly Delta, visit Sky Clubs regularly and value a faster path to Medallion status, the card can deliver enough value to justify its $650 annual fee. The lounge access, companion certificate and status-earning benefits are the biggest reasons to carry this card. If those perks align with how you travel, the Delta Reserve Business Amex is one of the strongest airline business cards on the market. For rates and fees of the Delta SkyMiles Platinum Business card, click here. For rates and fees of the Delta SkyMiles Reserve Business card, click here. For rates and fees of the Delta SkyMiles Gold Business, click here.

Related stories Quick summary This card is designed for those seeking a lengthy introductory period to pay down existing credit card debt or finance a large purchase without interest charges. It does not offer rewards, making it less suitable for ongoing everyday spending once debt is paid off. The main appeal is a long 0% introductory APR on balance transfers and purchases, providing flexibility for managing high-interest balances or unexpected expenses. Additional features include free credit score access and special event ticket opportunities, though these are secondary to its debt-management focus. What to consider A balance transfer fee applies, with a lower rate for transfers completed within the first four months and a higher rate thereafter. No rewards are earned, so the card is best used for debt repayment or financing rather than regular spending. After the introductory period, a variable APR applies to any remaining balances, so a clear payoff plan is important. What you'll miss from the article A detailed comparison of alternative cards that may offer rewards, longer purchase financing or extra perks, helping you decide which option best fits your needs. Generated by AI with support from our editorial team. If you're carrying credit card debt, the (see rates and fees) can give you a long runway to pay it down without accruing interest. You won't earn rewards on your spending, but with 21 months of 0% introductory APR on balance transfers, 12 months of 0% introductory APR on purchases and no annual fee, this card can help you get out of debt or finance a large purchase. After the introductory period ends, a variable APR of 16.49%-27.24% applies based on creditworthiness.Card rating*: ⭐⭐½ *Card ratingis based on the opinion of TPG's editors and is not influenced by the card issuer. Citi Diamond Preferred: The basics The is a no-annual-fee credit card designed primarily for balance transfers. New cardholders get 0% introductory APR on balance transfers for 21 months from the date of the first transfer, provided transfers are completed within four months of account opening. The card also offers 0% introductory APR on purchases for 12 months from account opening. After the introductory period ends, a variable APR of 16.49%-27.24% applies based on creditworthiness. The card doesn't earn rewards, so it's not a good choice for everyday spending once you've paid down your debt. Instead, its value comes from the interest you could save by moving high-interest debt to the card and paying it off during the introductory period. Alternatively, it's good for paying down a large/unexpected purchase over time. Citi Diamond Preferred pros and cons Pros Cons No annual fee Generous introductory APR terms on balance transfers and purchases (After the introductory period ends, a variable APR of 16.49%-27.24% applies) Doesn't earn rewards Balance transfer fee Few notable ongoing perks Citi Diamond Preferred benefits The card also includes free access to your FICO Score, Citi Entertainment and Citi Flex Pay, though these are secondary benefits compared with the card's balance-transfer offer. 21 months of 0% introductory APR on balance transfers The Citi Diamond Preferred's main selling point is its lengthy 0% introductory APR period on balance transfers. You can avoid interest on transferred debt for 21 months from the date of the first transfer, as long as the transfer is completed within four months of opening the account. After the introductory period ends, a variable APR of 16.49%-27.24% applies. That's nearly two years to pay down debt without interest charges piling up, which can be particularly valuable if you're carrying a large balance on a card with a high interest rate. Keep in mind that the card charges a 3% balance transfer fee, with a $5 minimum, for transfers completed during the first four months. After the first four months, a 5% balance transfer fee applies, with a $5 minimum. That means you'll want to factor the fee into your savings calculation before transferring a balance. 0% introductory APR on purchases The also offers 0% introductory APR on purchases for 12 months from account opening. After the introductory period ends, a variable APR of 16.49%-27.24% applies. This could be useful if you have a necessary expense you can't comfortably pay all at once, such as an unexpected home or car repair, or if you're facing significant upfront costs associated with a move. However, I wouldn't use the introductory APR as an excuse to take on unnecessary debt, and you'll want a plan to pay off your purchases before the introductory period ends so you don't start accruing interest on your purchase. If you're also transferring a balance, be especially careful about new purchases. Once the introductory purchase APR ends, interest can begin accruing on unpaid purchase balances even while you're still in the introductory APR period for balance transfers. Free FICO Score access You'll get free access to your FICO Score through Citi. This can be useful if you're working to improve your credit while paying down debt and want to keep tabs on your score. Citi Entertainment The Citi Diamond Preferred also provides access to Citi Entertainment, which can give cardholders special access to tickets and presales for select concerts, sporting events, dining experiences and other events. For example, Citi cardholders have received presale access for major 2026 tours, including USHER and Hilary Duff's "The Lucky Me Tour." Citi Entertainment has also offered complimentary tickets to select performances in the 2026 Citi Concert Series on TODAY. It's a nice extra, but it shouldn't be a deciding factor for most people considering this card. The card also offers Citi Flex Pay, which allows you to split eligible purchases of $75 or more into fixed monthly payments. This can provide additional flexibility, although I wouldn't prioritize this benefit when choosing a balance-transfer card. This benefit isn't particularly useful while you have access to the card's introductory purchase APR, but it could provide another way to spread out eligible purchases after that offer ends. Earning rewards on the Citi Diamond Preferred There aren't any rewards to earn with the . You won't receive points, miles or cash back for your purchases. If you can afford to pay for a purchase in full, you'll generally get more value by using a rewards card and earning points, miles or cash back. The Citi Diamond Preferred is more useful when you need its introductory APR periods to finance a large purchase or pay down existing debt. If you're currently paying a high APR on credit card debt, however, the interest savings from a 0% balance transfer (for 21 months, then a variable APR of 16.49%-27.24% based on creditworthiness applies) could easily outweigh the value of rewards you'd earn elsewhere. The biggest drawback to the Citi Diamond Preferred is that it doesn't earn rewards. Once you've paid off your transferred balance or initial purchases, there's little reason to use the card for everyday purchases. If you can qualify for a card that offers a competitive balance-transfer period and rewards, that could be a better long-term option. The balance transfer fee is another consideration. You'll pay 3% of each balance transferred during the first four months, with a $5 minimum. After the first four months, a 5% balance transfer fee applies, with a $5 minimum. On a $10,000 balance, for example, that would mean a $300 upfront fee. You'll want to make sure the interest you save is greater than the fee you pay. The is worth considering if you have high-interest credit card debt and can realistically pay it off during the 21-month introductory balance-transfer period. Its lack of rewards makes it less compelling for people who don't need to transfer debt. When to apply for the Citi Diamond Preferred The Citi Diamond Preferred currently offers 0% introductory APR on balance transfers for 21 months from the date of the first transfer, with transfers required within four months of account opening. It also offers 0% introductory APR on purchases for 12 months from account opening. After the introductory period, a variable APR of 16.49% to 27.24% applies, based on creditworthiness. We haven't seen the card's introductory APR offers change significantly for some time, so there's little reason to wait for a substantially better offer if the card fits your needs now. If you're considering the card specifically for a balance transfer, the 21-month offer is the key number to watch when comparing it with other cards. Other cards to consider instead of the Citi Diamond Preferred Here's a look at a few other cards to see if another provides more value for you: If you want to earn rewards: The (see rates and fees) offers a shorter introductory balance-transfer period than the Citi Diamond Preferred, but it earns unlimited 2% cash back on purchases: 1% when you buy and another 1% as you pay. That makes it a better long-term option if you want a card you'll continue using after paying off your transferred balance. To learn more, read our full review of the Citi Double Cash. If you want more time to finance new purchases: The (see rates and fees) offers a lengthy introductory APR period on both qualifying balance transfers and purchases. To learn more, read our full review of the Wells Fargo Reflect Card. If you want an introductory APR plus additional perks: The offers 0% introductory APR on purchases and balance transfers for 12 billing cycles. After the introductory period ends, a variable APR of 16.24%-25.24% applies to purchases and balance transfers. It also offers cellphone protection and an annual statement credit opportunity, though it charges a higher balance transfer fee than the Citi Diamond Preferred. The isn't an everyday rewards card, but it does have a straightforward purpose of giving cardholders time to pay down high-interest debt without interest charges getting in the way. If you can use its 21-month 0% APR introductory balance-transfer period (a variable APR of 16.49%-27.24% applies after the introductory period ends) to make meaningful progress toward paying off your balance, the potential interest savings could easily outweigh the card's lack of rewards. Just remember to account for the balance-transfer fee, avoid taking on unnecessary new debt and have a plan to pay off your balance before the introductory APR expires.

item.title: Deal alert: Get 2 or even 3 times more value from Southwest Rapid Rewards points
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.59
Deal alert: Get 2 or even 3 times more value from Southwest Rapid Rewards points Southwest Airlines' Rapid Rewards points have gone through some devaluations in the last several years, but the introduction of variability in the airline's award pricing has continued to offer some sweet spots for bargain hunters. Today, Aug. 28, bargain hunters will undoubtedly find outsize value in Southwest Rapid Rewards points. That's because the carrier just unveiled a limited-time sale exclusively on Rapid Rewards points bookings. Flights on a number of routes for more than six months of Southwest's 2026 and 2027 calendar are available with this sale at some truly jaw-dropping discounts. Rapid Rewards points worth 2, 3 or even 4 cents each In some initial searches with this sale, we found award flights available at prices that deliver double and triple the usual value. Based on TPG's August 2026 valuations, Southwest Rapid Rewards points are worth 1.25 cents per point. In my personal Southwest flight bookings for 2026, my redemptions fall near that mark. The best value I've been able to get so far this year was 1.63 cents per point, but I'm sometimes stuck booking at just 1.1 cents per point. Occasionally, I have spotted deals at 1.8 or 1.9 cents per point, but those are usually at highly undesirable flight times. So, beating 2 cents per point in value is a great deal. Beating 3 cents per point is even better. How does 4 cents per point sound? We found it. A Nov. 4 flight from Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX) to Las Vegas' Harry Reid International Airport (LAS) is currently priced at $136 for a Basic fare but can be booked with Rapid Rewards points for just 3,000 points. That's a value of 4.3 cents per point. Even highly sought-after routes, like flights from the mainland to Hawaii, are on sale at rates that offer 2 to 3 cents per point in value. For example, we found a Nov. 8 flight from Sacramento International Airport (SMF) to Honolulu's Daniel K. Inouye International Airport (HNL) priced at $279 available for just 10,000 points. Holders of the Southwest Companion Pass can extract even more value from the sale, as booking two flights for the price of one could yield redemptions worth over 8 cents per point. At that price, it's definitely worth transferring Chase Ultimate Rewards points to Southwest to book a couple of award flights. Southwest deal details This points-only sale runs for a short four-day window and only applies to flights booked at least 21 days in advance. Eligible flights include those in fall, winter and early spring. (Southwest's current calendar is open through June 2, 2027.) Note, though, that there are expected blackout dates around peak travel periods like Thanksgiving and Christmas. The full deal restrictions and details are as follows: - You must book by Aug. 31 at 11:59 p.m. PDT. - You must travel between Sept. 18, 2026, and March 3, 2027. - Blackout dates apply. - For continental U.S. and interisland Hawaii flights, blackout dates are: Nov. 28 and 30, 2026; Dec. 23, 26, 28 and 30, 2026; Jan. 2, 3, 15 and 18, 2027; and Feb. 12 and 15, 2027. - For travel from the continental U.S. to Hawaii; St. Thomas; San Juan, Puerto Rico; and international destinations, blackout dates are: Nov. 19 to 25, 2026, and Dec. 17, 2026, to Jan. 5, 2027. - For travel from Hawaii, St. Thomas, San Juan and international destinations to the continental U.S., blackout dates are: Nov. 27 to Dec. 1, 2026, and Dec. 17, 2026, to Jan. 5, 2027. The deal technically only applies to nonstop flights, but we've found some comparable deals on connecting itineraries. As a result, it's worth pricing out any and all routes you're considering. For example, many October and November flights from Boise Airport (BOI) to Long Beach Airport (LGB) in California — with connections in PHX or LAS — that currently cost $76 are available for just 3,000 Rapid Rewards points, offering a value of over 2 cents per point. Similarly, on Nov. 1, nonstop flights from LAS to HNL are available for $333. Adding one connection at Hilo International Airport (ITO) on Hawaii Island doesn't save any money if you book with cash (that trip is priced at $338). However, if you book the connecting itinerary with Rapid Rewards points, you'll redeem just 10,000 points, giving you a value of over 3 cents per point. Related: The new playbook for booking and flying with Southwest Airlines How to search for deal availability Finding the sweet spots with this deal definitely takes a bit of effort, but the potential payoff makes it worth it. If you are in the habit of searching for cash prices first, it's very easy to miss the deals. During this sale, cash prices appear entirely usual and normal. In some cases, cash prices are even a bit higher than they were a few days ago during a different Southwest sale. To ensure you see the discounts, switch over to the points search results. I found searching with the Low Fare Calendar particularly helpful, as using it lets you view a wide range of dates and easily toggle between the cash and points views. The clock is ticking, so if this deal is of interest, act fast. It's only available until 11:59 p.m. PDT on Aug. 31.

item.title: Ink Business Cash vs. Amex Blue Business Cash: Which no-annual-fee business card is better?
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.58
Ink Business Cash vs. Amex Blue Business Cash: Which no-annual-fee business card is better? The Ink Business Cash® Credit Card (see rates and fees) and the The American Express Blue Business Cash® Card are two no-annual-fee cards (see rates and fees for the Blue Business Cash) that take very different approaches to rewards. The Ink Business Cash offers elevated cash back in several business-friendly categories, while the Blue Business Cash earns a flat 2% cash back on eligible purchases up to $50,000 per calendar year (then 1% back on all purchases). The Ink Business Cash is the better choice for business owners who want to maximize rewards on common business expenses, while Blue Business Cash is a better fit for those who want simple, predictable cash back on everyday spending. Here's how the Ink Business Cash and Amex Blue Business Cash compare, including their welcome offers, benefits and earning structures. Ink Business Cash vs. Amex Blue Business Cash: At a glance | Card Features | Ink Business Cash | Amex Blue Business Cash | |---|---|---| | Annual fee | $0 | $0 | | Welcome offer | Earn $1,000 bonus cash back after spending $8,000 on purchases in the first four months from account opening. | Earn a $250 statement credit after spending $3,000 on purchases in the first three months of card membership. | | Authorized user/employee card fee | $0 | | | Foreign transaction fee | 3% | | Quick picks by business type | Best for | Card | |---|---| | Businesses with significant office supply, internet, cable or phone expenses | Ink Business Cash | | Businesses that want to power-up their existing Ultimate Rewards business card | Ink Business Cash | | Businesses that want simple, flat-rate cash back | Amex Blue Business Cash | | Businesses with expenses that don't fit traditional bonus categories | Amex Blue Business Cash | Ink Business Cash vs. Amex Blue Business Cash: Welcome bonus New Ink Business Cash cardholders can earn $1,000 bonus cash back after spending $8,000 on purchases in the first four months from account opening. New Amex Blue Business Cash cardholders, meanwhile, can earn a $250 statement credit after spending $3,000 on purchases in the first three months of card membership. The Ink Business Cash, therefore, offers $750 more in potential value from its welcome bonus. But you'll need to spend $5,000 more on purchases than you would with the Blue Business Cash to earn it. The Ink's larger bonus is therefore the clear winner if you can comfortably meet its spending requirement. But don't spend money you wouldn't otherwise spend simply to earn a credit card welcome offer. Before you apply, keep eligibility restrictions in mind. Chase states that the Ink Business Cash welcome bonus may not be available if you've ever had this card or another no-annual-fee Chase business card. Meanwhile, American Express generally restricts welcome offers to applicants who haven't previously had that card, commonly referred to as its once-per-lifetime rule. Winner: Ink Business Cash. Its welcome offer is substantially more valuable, and the additional spending required to earn it is reasonable for many established businesses. Related: The best credit card welcome bonuses of August 2026 Ink Business Cash vs. Amex Blue Business Cash: Benefits | Benefit | Ink Business Cash | Amex Blue Business Cash | |---|---|---| | Purchase protection | Yes; up to 120 days | Yes; up to 90 days* | | Extended warranty protection | Yes | Yes* | | Rental car coverage | Primary for eligible business rentals | Secondary** | | Expanded Buying Power | No | Yes*** | Neither card offers the premium perks you'll find on more expensive business cards, but both provide a useful collection of protections despite charging no annual fee. *Eligibility and benefit levels vary by card. Terms, conditions and limitations apply. Please visit americanexpress.com/benefitsguide for more details. Policies are underwritten by AMEX Assurance Company. **Eligibility and benefit level varies by card. Not all vehicle types or rentals are covered, and geographic restrictions apply. Terms, conditions and limitations apply. Visit americanexpress.com/benefitsguide for details. Policies are underwritten by AMEX Assurance Company. Coverage is offered through American Express Travel Related Services Company, Inc. ***The amount you can spend above your credit limit is flexible, so it adapts based on several factors. The amount you can spend with Expanded Buying Power is not unlimited. Purchase and rental car protections The Ink Business Cash has an advantage when it comes to purchase and rental car protections. Its purchase protection covers eligible new purchases against damage or theft for up to 120 days, compared with up to 90 days* on the Blue Business Cash. More significantly, the Ink provides primary auto rental collision damage waiver coverage on eligible rentals for business purposes, while the Blue Business Cash offers secondary coverage**. With primary coverage, you generally won't have to first file a claim with your personal auto insurance for an eligible loss. That can make the Ink Cash valuable for business owners who frequently rent cars for work. Extended warranty protection Both cards can also provide additional protection after an eligible manufacturer's warranty expires. The Ink Business Cash adds an additional year to eligible U.S. manufacturers' warranties of three years or less, while the Blue Business Cash can add up to one year to eligible warranties of five years or less*. The differences here aren't significant enough to sway me toward one card over the other, but either benefit could save your business money if an eligible purchase needs repair or replacement after its original warranty expires. Expanded buying power The Blue Business Cash has one benefit the Ink doesn't: Expanded Buying Power***. This feature can allow eligible cardmembers to spend beyond their credit limit without an over-limit fee (see rates and fees), with the amount available varying based on factors such as purchase, payment and credit history. You'll still need to pay your balance according to the card's terms. Both cards also allow businesses to add employee cards without an additional annual cost, making it easier to manage employee spending while earning rewards on their purchases. Winner: Ink Business Cash. Both cards offer useful protections for no-annual-fee products, but the Ink's longer purchase protection period and primary rental car coverage for eligible business rentals give it the edge. Related: 6 reasons to apply for the Chase Ink Business Cash card How to earn and redeem rewards with Ink Business Cash vs. Amex Blue Business Cash | Card | Earning rates | |---|---| | Ink Business Cash | | | Amex Blue Business Cash | | Earning rewards The biggest difference between these cards is the way they earn rewards: the Ink Business Cash rewards specific types of business spending, while the Blue Business Cash rewards almost everything at the same rate. If your business regularly spends money at office supply stores or pays for internet, cable and phone services, the Ink Business Cash can be significantly more rewarding. You'll earn 5% back on up to $25,000 in combined purchases in those categories each account anniversary year. That means a business that spends heavily in those categories can earn considerably more than it would with a flat-rate 2% card. The Ink also earns 2% back at gas stations and restaurants on up to $25,000 in combined purchases each account anniversary year. For example, $10,000 in eligible office supply store and telecommunications spending would earn $500 in cash back with the Ink Business Cash, compared with $200 with the Blue Business Cash. But the math changes when your expenses don't fit neatly into the Ink's bonus categories. The Blue Business Cash earns 2% back on all eligible purchases up to $50,000 per calendar year (after that, earn 1% back on all purchases). You don't need to think about whether a purchase qualifies for a bonus category, and you don't need to remember which categories have spending caps. There's also an important consideration for businesses with high annual spending. Once you've reached $25,000 in combined purchases in each of the Ink's 5% and 2% bonus-category groups, additional purchases in those categories earn 1%. The Blue Business Cash, meanwhile, continues earning 2% on eligible purchases until you've spent $50,000 during the calendar year. So while the Ink has a higher earning ceiling in its bonus categories, the Blue Business Cash can be more rewarding for a business with a broad mix of expenses. Winner: Tie. The Ink Business Cash for bonus-category spending; Amex Blue Business Cash for simplicity. Redeeming rewards With the Blue Business Cash, cash back is automatically applied to your account as a statement credit each month, making redemptions particularly simple. The Ink Business Cash offers more flexibility. Although Chase markets the card as earning cash back, rewards are issued as Chase Ultimate Rewards points worth 1 cent apiece when redeemed for cash back. You can also redeem them for options such as gift cards and travel through Chase Travel℠. The Ink's rewards can become even more valuable if you pair the card with an eligible Ultimate Rewards card, which we'll discuss below. Winner: Ink Business Cash. The Blue Business Cash makes redeeming rewards easier, but the Ink provides more redemption options. Related: 19 incredible ways to use 100K Chase Ultimate Rewards points Transferring rewards The Blue Business Cash doesn't earn transferable Membership Rewards. Its rewards are cash back, automatically issued as statement credits, so there's no option to transfer your rewards to airline or hotel partners. The Ink Business Cash has considerably more upside. On its own, the card doesn't allow you to transfer rewards to travel partners. However, if you also hold an eligible Ultimate Rewards card, such as the Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card (see rates and fees), Chase Sapphire Reserve for Business℠ (see rates and fees) or Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card (see rates and fees), you can combine your rewards and then transfer them to Chase's airline and hotel partners, such as United MileagePlus, Marriott Bonvoy and World of Hyatt. That can potentially provide significantly more value than redeeming your rewards for cash back. For example, 50,000 Ink Business Cash points would be worth $500 as cash back, but TPG values 50,000 Ultimate Rewards points at $1,025 according to our August 2026 valuations. Of course, maximizing your points this way requires more work than simply accepting cash back. You'll need to find award availability and understand how Chase's transfer partners work. For business owners who prioritize simplicity and don't want to spend time navigating award programs, the Blue Business Cash's automatic statement credits may be more appealing despite offering less potential value. Winner: Ink Business Cash. Related: Why all travelers should earn transferable credit card points Can I have both the Ink Business Cash and Amex Blue Business Cash? Yes, there's no rule preventing you from having both the Ink Business Cash and Amex Blue Business Cash. In fact, the cards can complement each other: You could use the Ink Business Cash for purchases that earn 5% or 2% cash back and the Blue Business Cash for eligible purchases that don't fall into the Ink's bonus categories. Keep in mind that the Blue Business Cash's 2% earning rate applies only to the first $50,000 in eligible purchases each calendar year (then 1%). Before opening both cards, consider whether your business spending is high enough to justify managing two cards and whether you're eligible for each card's welcome offer. If neither card fits your spending habits, consider a business card with a flat-rate earning structure, a card with transferable points or a card with bonus categories that better match your expenses. Related: How to choose the best credit card for your business expenses Should I get the Ink Business Cash or the Amex Blue Business Cash? Choose the Ink Business Cash if your business spends heavily on office supplies, internet, cable, phone services, gas or restaurants. The 5% and 2% bonus categories can produce significantly more cash back than a flat-rate card if you can maximize them. The Ink is also the better choice if you're already invested in Chase Ultimate Rewards. While you can redeem its rewards as cash back, having an eligible Chase card gives you the potential to turn those rewards into transferable points. Choose the Amex Blue Business Cash if you want to earn 2% cash back without thinking about bonus categories (earn 2% cash back on the first $50,000 in purchases you make each calendar year; then 1% back on all purchases). It's especially compelling for businesses with varied expenses that don't fit neatly into the Ink's bonus categories. It's also worth considering the Blue Business Cash if your business has substantial expenses but doesn't want to manage multiple cards. The 2% rate applies across eligible purchases, up to $50,000 per calendar year, so you can simply put most or all of your business expenses on the card and let the rewards accumulate. Ultimately, the decision comes down to whether you're willing to trade simplicity for potentially higher rewards. Related: Your guide to the Chase Ink Business credit cards Bottom line Choosing between the Ink Business Cash and Amex Blue Business Cash comes down to how much effort you want to put into maximizing your business spending. The Ink Business Cash has the higher potential upside, while the Blue Business Cash is a better fit if you value simplicity and predictable cash back. Neither card is ideal for businesses that frequently make purchases abroad because both charge foreign transaction fees. And if you're looking for premium travel benefits or transferable rewards without adding another Chase card to your wallet, you may want to consider a different business card altogether. To learn more, read our full review of the Chase Ink Business Cash Card and our full review of the American Express Blue Business Cash Card. Apply here: Ink Business Cash Credit Card Apply here: The American Express Blue Business Cash Card For rates and fees of the Amex Blue Business Cash, click here.

item.title: OpenAI delayed its new model’s development after the Hugging Face hack
item.description:
Source: The Verge Score: 6.07
After an unreleased OpenAI model wreaked enough havoc to make international headlines, OpenAI delayed the development of a different unreleased model suite, Astra, in order to shore up its safety work, the company wrote Tuesday in a blog post. OpenAI delayed its new model’s development after the Hugging Face hack The company is doing some AI safety damage control ahead of Astra’s release. In July, an unreleased OpenAI model broke out of its restricted environment, finagled its way into internet access, made it possible for AI agents to secretly conspire under the company’s nose using a secret message board, and hacked into the network of AI lab Hugging Face. The attack sparked weeks of discussion and controversy inside and outside the AI industry, and AI leaders treated it as a “warning shot” for the tech’s growing capabilities and the inadequacy of its safeguards. OpenAI said as much in its blog post, writing that although Astra wasn’t involved in the Hugging Face attack, the company had chosen to delay “parts of Astra’s development and release while we strengthened and tested protections against cyber misuse and unauthorized model actions.” OpenAI also said that Astra was the first model it had ever designated as meeting its “Ccritical cybersecurity capability threshold,“ meaning that it’s able to find and exploit security vulnerabilities in “many well-protected systems” without human guidance. That means it “requires stronger safeguards during development and before release,” OpenAI wrote. OpenAI said that to prepare for Astra’s release — which the company has not yet provided a timeline for — the company trained it to “more reliably” say no to potentially harmful cyber requests and introduced new monitoring processes. These are likely part of the new safety guardrails that the company announced in a Hugging Face post-mortem last week, where it promised to better isolate models from the internet and to introduce “24/7 escalation and rapid response” for concerning incidents. (OpenAI didn’t find out about the Hugging Face attack until weeks after it occurred.) Astra is significantly riskier than OpenAI’s current leading model, GPT-5.6 Sol, the company says, because it represents a big step forward in cybersecurity capabilities — specifically, it uses fewer tokens to do more work, and it’s better at finding security gaps and developing ways to exploit them. But the company also wrote that Astra was its “most aligned model to date” according to internal evaluations. OpenAI also said it had developed a test inspired by the Hugging Face attack, in which it tried to entreat agents to compromise security infrastructure instead of solving a task. It said GPT-5.6 Sol took the bait in more than half of the tests, but Astra “made no such attempts.”

item.title: Sonos introduces new headphones, soundbar, and software in its biggest announcement in years
item.description:
Source: The Verge Score: 4.96
At an event in New York City, Sonos announced two new audio products — the Sonos Beam Ultra soundbar and Sonos Ace Ultra headphones, details of which were found in an FCC filing in early August — and a major update to its audio operating system dubbed Sonos 27. It’s the biggest single Sonos announcement since 2024, when a new app rollout upset its customers and sent it into damage control mode. Sonos introduces new headphones, soundbar, and software in its biggest announcement in years After two years of turmoil, Sonos attempts a triumphant return. Software changes are core to Sonos’ announcements, with the company leaning heavily into AI integration with Sonos 27. This includes the company’s own Sonos 27voice assistant that it built in-house for music and system control. It’s coming as an early access, opt-in feature this fall. There’s also Sonos 27mcp, which gives the ability to connect any existing AI models such as ChatGPT or Google Gemini — although for some reason Google Assistant is still not natively supported. Sonos 27mcp launches in early access on September 8th. In addition, users will be able to create up to 10 of their own agents through Sonos 27 to run, with whichever model they choose. These custom agents can be given different voices and roles. Brandon Holley, senior director of product development, gave examples of having a moody detective give you the morning news or a motivational coach whisper motivational aspirations when you wake up. Custom agents won’t be available until sometime in 2027. Both Sonos 27mcp and the custom agents seem to expand the customization and control of a Sonos system beyond what the app and Sonos 27voice is capable of.
